id="cite_ref-122" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-122">&#91;122&#93;</a></sup> In 2015, Venezuela had the world's highest inflation rate with the rate surpassing 100%, which was the highest in the country's history.<sup id="cite_ref-FPblackbox_123-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FPblackbox-123">&#91;123&#93;</a></sup> In 2017, <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump" title="Donald Trump">Donald Trump</a>'s administration imposed more <a href="/wiki/Economic_sanctions" title="Economic sanctions">economic sanctions</a> against Venezuela's state-owned oil company <a href="/wiki/PDVSA" title="PDVSA">PDVSA</a> and Venezuelan officials.<sup id="cite_ref-124" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-124">&#91;124&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-125" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-125">&#91;125&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-126" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-126">&#91;126&#93;</a></sup> Economic problems, as well as crime and corruption, were some of the main causes of the <a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_protests_(2014%E2%80%93present)" class="mw-redirect" title="Venezuelan protests (2014–present)">2014–present Venezuelan protests</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-127" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-127">&#91;127&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-128" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-128">&#91;128&#93;</a></sup> Since 2014, roughly 5.6 million people have <a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_refugee_crisis" title="Venezuelan refugee crisis">fled Venezuela</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-129" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-129">&#91;129&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In January 2016, President Maduro decreed an "economic emergency", revealing the extent of the crisis and expanding his powers.<sup id="cite_ref-130" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-130">&#91;130&#93;</a></sup> In July 2016, Colombian border crossings were temporarily opened to allow Venezuelans to purchase food and basic household and health items in Colombia.<sup id="cite_ref-Venezuelans_Cross_Into_Colombia_In_Search_Of_Food_131-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Venezuelans_Cross_Into_Colombia_In_Search_Of_Food-131">&#91;131&#93;</a></sup> In September 2016, a study published in the Spanish-language <i><a href="/wiki/Diario_Las_Am%C3%A9ricas" title="Diario Las Américas">Diario Las Américas</a></i><sup id="cite_ref-Hambre_en_Venezuela:_El_15.7%_de_los_venezolanos_se_ha_alimentado_de_residuos_132-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hambre_en_Venezuela:_El_15.7%_de_los_venezolanos_se_ha_alimentado_de_residuos-132">&#91;132&#93;</a></sup> indicated that 15% of Venezuelans are eating "<a href="/wiki/Food_waste" class="mw-redirect" title="Food waste">food waste</a> discarded by commercial establishments". Close to 200 riots had occurred in Venezuelan prisons by October 2016, according to Una Ventana a la Libertad, an advocacy group for better prison conditions.<sup id="cite_ref-Man_claims_son_was_eaten_by_fellow_inmates_during_riot_in_Venezuelan_prison_133-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Man_claims_son_was_eaten_by_fellow_inmates_during_riot_in_Venezuelan_prison-133">&#91;133&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_TSJ_chamber_at_Maduro_2019_inauguration.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/The_TSJ_chamber_at_Maduro_2019_inauguration.jpg/220px-The_TSJ_chamber_at_Maduro_2019_inauguration.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/The_TSJ_chamber_at_Maduro_2019_inauguration.jpg/330px-The_TSJ_chamber_at_Maduro_2019_inauguration.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/The_TSJ_chamber_at_Maduro_2019_inauguration.jpg/440px-The_TSJ_chamber_at_Maduro_2019_inauguration.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2953" data-file-height="1969" /></a><figcaption>Maduro was <a href="/wiki/Second_inauguration_of_Nicol%C3%A1s_Maduro" title="Second inauguration of Nicolás Maduro">inaugurated</a> for a <a href="/wiki/2019_Venezuelan_presidential_crisis" class="mw-redirect" title="2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis">contested</a> and controversial second term on 10 January 2019.</figcaption></figure>
<p>In 2017, Venezuela experienced <a href="/wiki/2017_Venezuelan_constitutional_crisis" title="2017 Venezuelan constitutional crisis">a constitutional crisis in the country</a>. In March 2017, opposition leaders branded President Maduro a dictator after the Maduro-aligned <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Tribunal_of_Justice_(Venezuela)" title="Supreme Tribunal of Justice (Venezuela)">Supreme Tribunal</a>, which had been overturning most <a href="/wiki/National_Assembly_(Venezuela)" title="National Assembly (Venezuela)">National Assembly</a> decisions since the opposition took control of the body, took over the functions of the assembly, pushing a lengthy political standoff to new heights.<sup id="cite_ref-reuters-maduro_97-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-reuters-maduro-97">&#91;97&#93;</a></sup> The Supreme Court backed down and reversed its decision on 1 April 2017.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (March 2021)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> A month later, President Maduro announced the <a href="/wiki/2017_Venezuelan_Constituent_Assembly_election" title="2017 Venezuelan Constituent Assembly election">2017 Venezuelan Constituent Assembly election</a> and on 30 August 2017, the <a href="/wiki/2017_Constituent_National_Assembly" class="mw-redirect" title="2017 Constituent National Assembly">2017 Constituent National Assembly</a> was elected into office and quickly stripped the National Assembly of its powers.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (March 2021)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> The election raised concerns of an emerging dictatorship.<sup id="cite_ref-NYTjail_134-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NYTjail-134">&#91;134&#93;</a></sup> In December 2017, President Maduro declared that leading opposition parties would be barred from taking part in the following year's presidential vote after they boycotted mayoral polls.<sup id="cite_ref-135" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-135">&#91;135&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Maduro won the <a href="/wiki/2018_Venezuelan_presidential_election" title="2018 Venezuelan presidential election">2018 election</a> with 67.8% of the vote. The result was challenged by countries including Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Brazil, Canada, Germany, France and the United States who deemed it fraudulent and moved to recognize <a href="/wiki/Juan_Guaid%C3%B3" title="Juan Guaidó">Juan Guaidó</a> as president.<sup id="cite_ref-136" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-136">&#91;136&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-137" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-137">&#91;137&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-138" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-138">&#91;138&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-139" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-139">&#91;139&#93;</a></sup> Other countries continued to recognize Maduro as president,<sup id="cite_ref-140" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-140">&#91;140&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-141" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-141">&#91;141&#93;</a></sup> although China, facing financial pressure over its position, reportedly began hedging its position by decreasing loans given, cancelling joint ventures, and signaling willingness to work with all parties.<sup id="cite_ref-142" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-142">&#91;142&#93;</a></sup> In January 2019 the Permanent Council of the <a href="/wiki/Organization_of_American_States" title="Organization of American States">Organization of American States</a> (OAS) approved a resolution "to not recognize the legitimacy of Nicolas Maduro's new term as of the 10th of January of 2019".<sup id="cite_ref-143" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-143">&#91;143&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In August 2019, United States President <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump" title="Donald Trump">Donald Trump</a> signed an executive order to impose a total economic embargo against Venezuela.<sup id="cite_ref-144" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-144">&#91;144&#93;</a></sup> In March 2020, the Trump administration indicted Maduro and several Venezuelan officials, including the Chief Justice of the Supreme Tribunal, on charges of drug trafficking, <a href="/wiki/Narcoterrorism" title="Narcoterrorism">narcoterrorism</a>, and corruption.<sup id="cite_ref-145" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-145">&#91;145&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template noprint Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:No_original_research#Primary,_secondary_and_tertiary_sources" title="Wikipedia:No original research"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable secondary sources. (March 2021)">non-primary source needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p><p>In June 2020, a report by the US organisation <a href="/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights" title="Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights">Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights</a> documented <a href="/wiki/Enforced_disappearance" title="Enforced disappearance">enforced disappearances</a> in Venezuela that occurred in the years 2018 and 2019. During the period, 724 enforced disappearances of <a href="/wiki/Political_prisoner" title="Political prisoner">political detainees</a> were reported. The report stated that Venezuelan security forces subjected victims, who had been disappeared, to illegal interrogation processes <a href="/wiki/Torture_in_Venezuela" title="Torture in Venezuela">accompanied by torture</a> and cruel or inhuman treatment. The report stated that the Venezuelan government strategically used enforced disappearances to silence political opponents and other critical voices it deemed a threat.<sup id="cite_ref-146" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-146">&#91;146&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-147" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-147">&#91;147&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Geography">Geography</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Geography_of_Venezuela" title="Geography of Venezuela">Geography of Venezuela</a></div>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Venezuela_Topography.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Venezuela_Topography.png/300px-Venezuela_Topography.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="258" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Venezuela_Topography.png/450px-Venezuela_Topography.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Venezuela_Topography.png/600px-Venezuela_Topography.png 2x" data-file-width="2101" data-file-height="1809" /></a><figcaption>Topographic map of Venezuela</figcaption></figure>
<p>Venezuela is located in the north of South America; geologically, its mainland rests on the <a href="/wiki/South_American_Plate" title="South American Plate">South American Plate</a>. It has a total area of 916,445&#160;km<sup>2</sup> (353,841&#160;sq&#160;mi) and a land area of 882,050&#160;km<sup>2</sup> (340,560&#160;sq&#160;mi), making Venezuela the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_outlying_territories_by_total_area" class="mw-redirect" title="List of countries and outlying territories by total area">33rd largest country in the world</a>. The territory it controls lies between latitudes <a href="/wiki/Equator" title="Equator">0°</a> and <a href="/wiki/16th_parallel_north" title="16th parallel north">16°N</a> and longitudes <a href="/wiki/59th_meridian_west" title="59th meridian west">59°</a> and <a href="/wiki/74th_meridian_west" title="74th meridian west">74°W</a>.
</p><p>Shaped roughly like a triangle, the country has a 2,800&#160;km (1,700&#160;mi) coastline in the north, which includes numerous islands in the Caribbean and the northeast borders the northern Atlantic Ocean. Most observers describe Venezuela in terms of four fairly well defined <a href="/wiki/Topography" title="Topography">topographical</a> regions: the <a href="/wiki/Maracaibo_Basin" title="Maracaibo Basin">Maracaibo lowlands</a> in the northwest, the northern mountains extending in a broad east–west arc from the Colombian border along the northern Caribbean coast, the wide plains in central Venezuela, and the <a href="/wiki/Guiana_Highlands" class="mw-redirect" title="Guiana Highlands">Guiana Highlands</a> in the southeast.
</p><p>The northern mountains are the extreme northeastern extensions of South America's Andes mountain range. <a href="/wiki/Pico_Bol%C3%ADvar" title="Pico Bolívar">Pico Bolívar</a>, the nation's highest point at 4,979&#160;m (16,335&#160;ft), lies in this region. To the south, the dissected <a href="/wiki/Guayana_Region" class="mw-redirect" title="Guayana Region">Guiana Highlands</a> contain the northern fringes of the Amazon Basin and <a href="/wiki/Angel_Falls" title="Angel Falls">Angel Falls</a>, the world's highest waterfall, as well as <i><a href="/wiki/Tepui" title="Tepui">tepuis</a></i>, large table-like mountains. The country's center is characterized by the <i>llanos</i>, which are extensive plains that stretch from the Colombian border in the far west to the Orinoco River <a href="/wiki/River_delta" title="River delta">delta</a> in the east. The Orinoco, with its rich <a href="/wiki/Alluvium" title="Alluvium">alluvial soils</a>, binds the largest and most important <a href="/wiki/Drainage_system_(geomorphology)" title="Drainage system (geomorphology)">river system</a> of the country; it originates in one of the largest <a href="/wiki/Drainage_basin" title="Drainage basin">watersheds</a> in Latin America. The <a href="/wiki/Caron%C3%AD_River_(Venezuela)" class="mw-redirect" title="Caroní River (Venezuela)">Caroní</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Apure_River" title="Apure River">Apure</a> are other major rivers.
</p>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Guanaguanare.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/Guanaguanare.JPG/273px-Guanaguanare.JPG" decoding="async" width="273" height="205" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/Guanaguanare.JPG/410px-Guanaguanare.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/Guanaguanare.JPG/546px-Guanaguanare.JPG 2x" data-file-width="4320" data-file-height="3240" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Cayo_de_Agua" title="Cayo de Agua">Cayo de Agua</a>, <a href="/wiki/Los_Roques_Archipelago" title="Los Roques Archipelago">Los Roques</a> Archipiélago, <a href="/wiki/Caribbean_Sea" title="Caribbean Sea">Caribbean Sea</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Venezuela borders Colombia to the west, <a href="/wiki/Guyana" title="Guyana">Guyana</a> to the east, and Brazil to the south. Caribbean islands such as <a href="/wiki/Trinidad_and_Tobago" title="Trinidad and Tobago">Trinidad and Tobago</a>, <a href="/wiki/Grenada" title="Grenada">Grenada</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cura%C3%A7ao" title="Curaçao">Curaçao</a>, <a href="/wiki/Aruba" title="Aruba">Aruba</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Leeward_Antilles" title="Leeward Antilles">Leeward Antilles</a> lie near the Venezuelan coast. Venezuela has territorial disputes with Guyana, formerly United Kingdom, largely concerning the <a href="/wiki/Guayana_Esequiba" title="Guayana Esequiba">Essequibo area</a> and with Colombia concerning the <a href="/wiki/Gulf_of_Venezuela" title="Gulf of Venezuela">Gulf of Venezuela</a>. In 1895, after years of diplomatic attempts to solve the border dispute, the dispute over the Essequibo River border flared up. It was submitted to a "neutral" commission (composed of British, American, and Russian representatives and without a direct Venezuelan representative), which in 1899 decided mostly against Venezuela's claim.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (January 2023)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Climate">Climate</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Climate_of_Venezuela" title="Climate of Venezuela">Climate of Venezuela</a></div><p>Venezuela is entirely located in the tropics over the Equator to around 12° N. Its climate varies from humid low-elevation plains, where average annual temperatures range as high as 35&#160;°C (95.0&#160;°F), to glaciers and highlands (the <i><a href="/wiki/P%C3%A1ramo" title="Páramo">páramos</a></i>) with an average yearly temperature of 8&#160;°C (46.4&#160;°F). Annual rainfall varies from 430&#160;mm (16.9&#160;in) in the semiarid portions of the northwest to over 1,000&#160;mm (39.4&#160;in) in the Orinoco Delta of the far east and the Amazonian Jungle in the south. The precipitation level is lower in the period from August through April. These periods are referred to as hot-humid and cold-dry seasons. Another characteristic of the climate is this variation throughout the country by the existence of a mountain range called "Cordillera de la Costa" which crosses the country from east to west. The majority of the population lives in these mountains.<sup id="cite_ref-LOC_2005_148-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-LOC_2005-148">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup></p><figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Venezuela_K%C3%B6ppen.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Venezuela_K%C3%B6ppen.png/266px-Venezuela_K%C3%B6ppen.png" decoding="async" width="266" height="216" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Venezuela_K%C3%B6ppen.png/399px-Venezuela_K%C3%B6ppen.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Venezuela_K%C3%B6ppen.png/532px-Venezuela_K%C3%B6ppen.png 2x" data-file-width="4782" data-file-height="3891" /></a><figcaption>Venezuela map of Köppen climate classification</figcaption></figure>
<p>The country falls into four horizontal temperature zones based primarily on elevation, having tropical, dry, temperate with dry winters, and polar (<a href="/wiki/Alpine_tundra" title="Alpine tundra">alpine tundra</a>) climates, amongst others.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEWarhol200665_149-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWarhol200665-149">&#91;149&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Geografía_–_Clima_150-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Geografía_–_Clima-150">&#91;150&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-151" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-151">&#91;151&#93;</a></sup> In the tropical zone—below 800&#160;m (2,625&#160;ft)—temperatures are hot, with yearly averages ranging between 26 and 28&#160;°C (78.8 and 82.4&#160;°F). The temperate zone ranges between 800 and 2,000&#160;m (2,625 and 6,562&#160;ft) with averages from 12 to 25&#160;°C (53.6 to 77.0&#160;°F); many of Venezuela's cities, including the capital, lie in this region. Colder conditions with temperatures from 9 to 11&#160;°C (48.2 to 51.8&#160;°F) are found in the cool zone between 2,000 and 3,000&#160;m (6,562 and 9,843&#160;ft), especially in the Venezuelan Andes, where pastureland and permanent snowfield with yearly averages below 8&#160;°C (46&#160;°F) cover land above 3,000 meters (9,843&#160;ft) in the <i>páramos</i>.
</p><p>The highest temperature recorded was 42&#160;°C (108&#160;°F) in <a href="/wiki/Machiques" title="Machiques">Machiques</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-152" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-152">&#91;152&#93;</a></sup> and the lowest temperature recorded was −11&#160;°C (12&#160;°F), reported from an uninhabited high altitude at <a href="/wiki/Pico_Piedras_Blancas" title="Pico Piedras Blancas">Páramo de Piedras Blancas</a> (<a href="/wiki/M%C3%A9rida_state" class="mw-redirect" title="Mérida state">Mérida state</a>).<sup id="cite_ref-153" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-153">&#91;153&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Biodiversity_and_conservation">Biodiversity and conservation</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Natural_regions_of_Venezuela" title="Natural regions of Venezuela">Natural regions of Venezuela</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fauna_of_Venezuela" title="Fauna of Venezuela">Fauna of Venezuela</a>, <a href="/wiki/Flora_of_Venezuela" title="Flora of Venezuela">Flora of Venezuela</a>, <a href="/wiki/National_symbols_of_Venezuela" title="National symbols of Venezuela">National symbols of Venezuela</a>, <a href="/wiki/List_of_birds_of_Venezuela" title="List of birds of Venezuela">List of birds of Venezuela</a>, <a href="/wiki/Environmental_issues_in_Venezuela" title="Environmental issues in Venezuela">Environmental issues in Venezuela</a>, and <a href="/wiki/List_of_national_parks_of_Venezuela" title="List of national parks of Venezuela">List of national parks of Venezuela</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Curacao-Icterus-Icterus-2013.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Curacao-Icterus-Icterus-2013.JPG/220px-Curacao-Icterus-Icterus-2013.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="166" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Curacao-Icterus-Icterus-2013.JPG/330px-Curacao-Icterus-Icterus-2013.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Curacao-Icterus-Icterus-2013.JPG/440px-Curacao-Icterus-Icterus-2013.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2649" data-file-height="1995" /></a><figcaption>The national animal of Venezuela is the <a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_troupial" title="Venezuelan troupial">troupial (Icterus icterus)</a>,</figcaption></figure>
<p>Venezuela lies within the <a href="/wiki/Neotropical_realm" title="Neotropical realm">Neotropical realm</a>; large portions of the country were originally covered by <a href="/wiki/Tropical_and_subtropical_moist_broadleaf_forests" title="Tropical and subtropical moist broadleaf forests">moist broadleaf forests</a>. One of 17 <a href="/wiki/Megadiverse_countries" title="Megadiverse countries">megadiverse countries</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-154" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-154">&#91;154&#93;</a></sup> Venezuela's <a href="/wiki/Habitat" title="Habitat">habitats</a> range from the Andes Mountains in the west to the Amazon Basin rainforest in the south, via extensive <i>llanos</i> plains and Caribbean coast in the center and the Orinoco River Delta in the east. They include <a href="/wiki/Deserts_and_xeric_shrublands" title="Deserts and xeric shrublands">xeric scrublands</a> in the extreme northwest and coastal <a href="/wiki/Mangrove" title="Mangrove">mangrove</a> forests in the northeast.<sup id="cite_ref-LOC_2005_148-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-LOC_2005-148">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> Its <a href="/wiki/Cloud_forest" title="Cloud forest">cloud forests</a> and lowland <a href="/wiki/Rainforest" title="Rainforest">rainforests</a> are particularly rich.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEDydynskiBeech200442_155-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDydynskiBeech200442-155">&#91;155&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Fauna_of_Venezuela" title="Fauna of Venezuela">Animals</a> of Venezuela are diverse and include <a href="/wiki/Manatee" title="Manatee">manatees</a>, <a href="/wiki/Three-toed_sloth" title="Three-toed sloth">three-toed sloth</a>, <a href="/wiki/Two-toed_sloth" title="Two-toed sloth">two-toed sloth</a>, <a href="/wiki/Amazon_river_dolphin" title="Amazon river dolphin">Amazon river dolphins</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Orinoco_Crocodile" class="mw-redirect" title="Orinoco Crocodile">Orinoco Crocodiles</a>, which have been reported to reach up to 6.6&#160;m (22&#160;ft) in length. Venezuela hosts a total of 1,417 bird species, 48 of which are endemic.<sup id="cite_ref-156" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-156">&#91;156&#93;</a></sup> Important birds include <a href="/wiki/Ibis" title="Ibis">ibises</a>, <a href="/wiki/Osprey" title="Osprey">ospreys</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kingfisher" title="Kingfisher">kingfishers</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEDydynskiBeech200442_155-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDydynskiBeech200442-155">&#91;155&#93;</a></sup> and the yellow-orange <a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_troupial" title="Venezuelan troupial">Venezuelan troupial</a>, the national bird. Notable <a href="/wiki/Mammal" title="Mammal">mammals</a> include the <a href="/wiki/Giant_anteater" title="Giant anteater">giant anteater</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jaguar" title="Jaguar">jaguar</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Capybara" title="Capybara">capybara</a>, the world's largest <a href="/wiki/Rodent" title="Rodent">rodent</a>. More than half of Venezuelan avian and mammalian species are found in the <a href="/wiki/Amazon_Rainforest" class="mw-redirect" title="Amazon Rainforest">Amazonian forests</a> south of the Orinoco.<sup id="cite_ref-Bevilacqua_2002_157-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bevilacqua_2002-157">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>For the fungi, an account was provided by R.W.G. Dennis<sup id="cite_ref-158" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-158">&#91;158&#93;</a></sup> which has been digitized and the records made available on-line as part of the Cybertruffle Robigalia database.<sup id="cite_ref-159" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-159">&#91;159&#93;</a></sup> That database includes nearly 3,900 species of fungi recorded from Venezuela, but is far from complete, and the true total number of fungal species already known from Venezuela is likely higher, given the generally accepted estimate that only about 7% of all fungi worldwide have so far been discovered.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTE&#39;&#39;Georgia_Country_Study_Guide_Volume_1_Strategic_Information_and_Developments&#39;&#39;201336_160-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTE&#39;&#39;Georgia_Country_Study_Guide_Volume_1_Strategic_Information_and_Developments&#39;&#39;201336-160">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Shakira_posando.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/Shakira_posando.JPG/217px-Shakira_posando.JPG" decoding="async" width="217" height="289" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/Shakira_posando.JPG/325px-Shakira_posando.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/Shakira_posando.JPG/433px-Shakira_posando.JPG 2x" data-file-width="600" data-file-height="800" /></a><figcaption>Crocodile in Hato El Cedral in <a href="/wiki/Apure_State" class="mw-redirect" title="Apure State">Apure State</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Among plants of Venezuela, over 25,000 species of <a href="/wiki/Orchidaceae" class="mw-redirect" title="Orchidaceae">orchids</a> are found in the country's cloud forest and lowland rainforest ecosystems.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEDydynskiBeech200442_155-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDydynskiBeech200442-155">&#91;155&#93;</a></sup> These include the <i>flor de mayo</i> orchid (<i><a href="/wiki/Cattleya_mossiae" title="Cattleya mossiae">Cattleya mossiae</a></i>), the national flower. Venezuela's national tree is the <a href="/wiki/Tabebuia_chrysantha" class="mw-redirect" title="Tabebuia chrysantha">araguaney</a>. The tops of the tepuis are also home to several carnivorous plants including the marsh pitcher plant, <a href="/wiki/Heliamphora" title="Heliamphora">Heliamphora</a>, and the insectivorous bromeliad, <a href="/wiki/Brocchinia_reducta" title="Brocchinia reducta">Brocchinia reducta</a>.
</p><p>Venezuela is among the top 20 countries in terms of <a href="/wiki/Endemism" title="Endemism">endemism</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-GFW_161-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-GFW-161">&#91;161&#93;</a></sup> Among its animals, 23% of <a href="/wiki/Reptile" title="Reptile">reptilian</a> and 50% of <a href="/wiki/Amphibian" title="Amphibian">amphibian</a> species, including the <a href="/wiki/Mannophryne_trinitatis" title="Mannophryne trinitatis">Trinidad poison frog</a>, are endemic.<sup id="cite_ref-GFW_161-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-GFW-161">&#91;161&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-162" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-162">&#91;162&#93;</a></sup> Although the available information is still very small, a first effort has been made to estimate the number of fungal species endemic to Venezuela: 1334 species of fungi have been tentatively identified as possibly endemic.<sup id="cite_ref-163" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-163">&#91;163&#93;</a></sup> Some 38% of the over 21,000 plant species known from Venezuela are unique to the country.<sup id="cite_ref-GFW_161-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-GFW-161">&#91;161&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Venezuela is one of the 10 most biodiverse countries on the planet, yet it is one of the leaders of deforestation due to economic and political factors. Each year, roughly 287,600 hectares of forest are permanently destroyed and other areas are degraded by mining, oil extraction, and logging. Between 1990 and 2005, Venezuela officially lost 8.3% of its forest cover, which is about 4.3&#160;million ha. In response, federal protections for critical habitat were implemented; for example, 20% to 33% of forested land is protected.<sup id="cite_ref-Bevilacqua_2002_157-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bevilacqua_2002-157">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup> Venezuela had a 2019 <a href="/wiki/Forest_Landscape_Integrity_Index" title="Forest Landscape Integrity Index">Forest Landscape Integrity Index</a> mean score of 8.78/10, ranking it 19th globally out of 172 countries.<sup id="cite_ref-164" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-164">&#91;164&#93;</a></sup> The country's <a href="/wiki/Biosphere_reserve" class="mw-redirect" title="Biosphere reserve">biosphere reserve</a> is part of the <a href="/wiki/World_Network_of_Biosphere_Reserves" title="World Network of Biosphere Reserves">World Network of Biosphere Reserves</a>; five <a href="/wiki/Wetlands" class="mw-redirect" title="Wetlands">wetlands</a> are registered under the <a href="/wiki/Ramsar_Convention" title="Ramsar Convention">Ramsar Convention</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-165" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-165">&#91;165&#93;</a></sup> In 2003, 70% of the nation's land was under conservation management in over 200 protected areas, including 43 national parks.<sup id="cite_ref-166" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-166">&#91;166&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/List_of_national_parks_of_Venezuela" title="List of national parks of Venezuela">Venezuela's 43 national parks</a> include Canaima National Park, <a href="/wiki/Morrocoy_National_Park" title="Morrocoy National Park">Morrocoy National Park</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Mochima_National_Park" title="Mochima National Park">Mochima National Park</a>. In the far south is a reserve for the country's Yanomami tribes. Covering 32,000 square miles (82,880 square kilometres), the area is off-limits to farmers, miners, and all non-Yanomami settlers.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:LakeVal.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/LakeVal.jpg/220px-LakeVal.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/LakeVal.jpg/330px-LakeVal.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/LakeVal.jpg/440px-LakeVal.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1024" data-file-height="768" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Valencia_Lake" class="mw-redirect" title="Valencia Lake">Valencia Lake</a>, formerly praised by <a href="/wiki/Alexander_von_Humboldt" title="Alexander von Humboldt">Alexander von Humboldt</a> for its beauty, is massively polluted due to the countless sewage systems pouring residuals.<sup id="cite_ref-167" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-167">&#91;167&#93;</a></sup></figcaption></figure><p>Venezuela was one of the few countries that did not enter an <a href="/wiki/Intended_Nationally_Determined_Contributions" class="mw-redirect" title="Intended Nationally Determined Contributions">INDC</a> at <a href="/wiki/COP21" class="mw-redirect" title="COP21">COP21</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-168" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-168">&#91;168&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-169" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-169">&#91;169&#93;</a></sup> Many terrestrial ecosystems are considered <a href="/wiki/IUCN_Red_List_of_Ecosystems#Risk_Categories" title="IUCN Red List of Ecosystems">endangered</a>, specially the <a href="/wiki/Dry_forest" class="mw-redirect" title="Dry forest">dry forest</a> in the northern regions of the country and the <a href="/wiki/Coral_reef" title="Coral reef">coral reefs</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Caribbean" title="Caribbean">Caribbean</a> coast.<sup id="cite_ref-Foundations_170-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Foundations-170">&#91;170&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-171" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-171">&#91;171&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-172" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-172">&#91;172&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>There are 105 protected areas in Venezuela, which cover around 26% of the country's continental, marine and insular surface.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (February 2022)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Hydrography">Hydrography</span></h3>
<p>The country is made up of three river basins: the <a href="/wiki/Caribbean_Sea" title="Caribbean Sea">Caribbean Sea</a>, the Atlantic Ocean and Lake Valencia, which forms an endorheic basin.<sup id="cite_ref-173" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-173">&#91;173&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On the Atlantic side it drains most of Venezuela's river waters. The largest basin in this area is the extensive Orinoco basin<sup id="cite_ref-174" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-174">&#91;174&#93;</a></sup> whose surface area, close to one million km<sup>2</sup>, is greater than that of the whole of Venezuela, although it has a presence of 65% in the country.
</p><p>The size of this basin - similar to that of the Danube - makes it the third largest in South America, and it gives rise to a flow of some 33,000 m³/s, making the Orinoco the third largest in the world, and also one of the most valuable from the point of view of renewable natural resources. The Rio or Brazo Casiquiare is unique in the world, as it is a natural derivation of the <a href="/wiki/Orinoco_river" class="mw-redirect" title="Orinoco river">Orinoco</a> that, after some 500&#160;km in length, connects it to the Negro River, which in turn is a tributary of the <a href="/wiki/Amazon_River" title="Amazon River">Amazon</a>. 
</p>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:LA_LAGUNA_VICTORIA.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/LA_LAGUNA_VICTORIA.JPG/229px-LA_LAGUNA_VICTORIA.JPG" decoding="async" width="229" height="153" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/LA_LAGUNA_VICTORIA.JPG/344px-LA_LAGUNA_VICTORIA.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/LA_LAGUNA_VICTORIA.JPG/458px-LA_LAGUNA_VICTORIA.JPG 2x" data-file-width="3872" data-file-height="2592" /></a><figcaption>Victoria Lagoon, <a href="/wiki/M%C3%A9rida_(state)" title="Mérida (state)">Mérida State</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The Orinoco receives directly or indirectly rivers such as the Ventuari, the Caura, the <a href="/wiki/Caron%C3%AD_River" title="Caroní River">Caroní</a>, the Meta, the <a href="/wiki/Arauca_River" title="Arauca River">Arauca</a>, the Apure and many others. Other Venezuelan rivers that empty into the Atlantic are the waters of the San Juan and Cuyuní basins. Finally, there is the Amazon River, which receives the Guainía, the Negro and others. Other basins are the <a href="/wiki/Gulf_of_Paria" title="Gulf of Paria">Gulf of Paria</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Essequibo_River" title="Essequibo River">Esequibo River</a>.
The second most important watershed is the Caribbean Sea. The rivers of this region are usually short and of scarce and irregular flow, with some exceptions such as the <a href="/wiki/Catatumbo_River" title="Catatumbo River">Catatumbo</a>, which originates in <a href="/wiki/Colombia" title="Colombia">Colombia</a> and drains into the Maracaibo Lake basin. Among the rivers that reach the Maracaibo lake basin are the Chama, the Escalante, the Catatumbo, and the contributions of the smaller basins of the Tocuyo, Yaracuy, Neverí and Manzanares rivers.
</p><p>
A minimum drains to the Lake Valencia basin.<sup id="cite_ref-175" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-175">&#91;175&#93;</a></sup> Of the total extension of the rivers, a total of 5400&#160;km are navigable. Other rivers worth mentioning are the Apure, Arauca, Caura, Meta, Barima, <a href="/wiki/Portuguesa_River" title="Portuguesa River">Portuguesa</a>, Ventuari and Zulia, among others.</p><figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Cerro_Wichuj(Cara_de_Indio)_(12111191594).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/Cerro_Wichuj%28Cara_de_Indio%29_%2812111191594%29.jpg/250px-Cerro_Wichuj%28Cara_de_Indio%29_%2812111191594%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/Cerro_Wichuj%28Cara_de_Indio%29_%2812111191594%29.jpg/375px-Cerro_Wichuj%28Cara_de_Indio%29_%2812111191594%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/Cerro_Wichuj%28Cara_de_Indio%29_%2812111191594%29.jpg/500px-Cerro_Wichuj%28Cara_de_Indio%29_%2812111191594%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4917" data-file-height="3278" /></a><figcaption>Amazon <a href="/wiki/Rainforest" title="Rainforest">rainforest</a> and Autana River, <a href="/wiki/Amazonas_(Venezuela)" class="mw-redirect" title="Amazonas (Venezuela)">Amazonas</a> state</figcaption></figure><p>The country's main lakes are Lake Maracaibo<sup id="cite_ref-176" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-176">&#91;176&#93;</a></sup> -the largest in South America- open to the sea through the natural channel, but with fresh water, and Lake Valencia with its endorheic system. Other noteworthy bodies of water are the <a href="/wiki/Guri_Reservoir" title="Guri Reservoir">Guri reservoir</a>, the Altagracia lagoon, the Camatagua reservoir and the Mucubají lagoon in the Andes.
</p><h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Relief">Relief</span></h3>
<p>The Venezuelan natural <a href="/wiki/Landscape" title="Landscape">landscape</a><sup id="cite_ref-:3_177-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-177">&#91;177&#93;</a></sup> is the product of the interaction of <a href="/wiki/Tectonic_plates" class="mw-redirect" title="Tectonic plates">tectonic plates</a><sup id="cite_ref-:3_177-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-177">&#91;177&#93;</a></sup> that since the <a href="/wiki/Paleozoic" title="Paleozoic">Paleozoic</a> have contributed to its current appearance. On the formed structures, seven physical-natural units have been modeled, differentiated in their relief and in their <a href="/wiki/Natural_resources" class="mw-redirect" title="Natural resources">natural resources</a>.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Flores_para_la_Nieve.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Flores_para_la_Nieve.JPG/220px-Flores_para_la_Nieve.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Flores_para_la_Nieve.JPG/330px-Flores_para_la_Nieve.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Flores_para_la_Nieve.JPG/440px-Flores_para_la_Nieve.JPG 2x" data-file-width="4896" data-file-height="3672" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Bol%C3%ADvar_Peak" class="mw-redirect" title="Bolívar Peak">Bolívar Peak</a>, the highest mountain in Venezuela</figcaption></figure>
<p>The relief of Venezuela has the following characteristics: <a href="/wiki/Coastline" class="mw-redirect" title="Coastline">coastline</a> with several peninsulas<sup id="cite_ref-178" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-178">&#91;178&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Islands" class="mw-redirect" title="Islands">islands</a>, adenas of the Andes mountain range (north and northwest), Lake Maracaibo (between the chains, on the coast);<sup id="cite_ref-:4_179-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:4-179">&#91;179&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Orinoco_river" class="mw-redirect" title="Orinoco river">Orinoco river</a> delta,<sup id="cite_ref-:5_180-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-180">&#91;180&#93;</a></sup> region of <a href="/wiki/Peneplain" title="Peneplain">peneplains</a> and plateaus (tepui, east of the Orinoco) that together form the Guyanas massif (plateaus, southeast of the country).
</p><p>The oldest rock formations in South America are found in the complex basement of the Guyanas highlands<sup id="cite_ref-:6_181-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:6-181">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup> and in the crystalline line of the Maritime and Cordillera massifs in Venezuela. The Venezuelan part of the Guyanas <a href="/wiki/Altiplano" title="Altiplano">Altiplano</a> consists of a large granite block of <a href="/wiki/Gneiss" title="Gneiss">gneiss</a> and other crystalline <a href="/wiki/Archean" title="Archean">Archean</a> rocks, with underlying layers of sandstone and shale clay.<sup id="cite_ref-182" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-182">&#91;182&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The core of <a href="/wiki/Granite" title="Granite">granite</a> and <a href="/wiki/Cordillera" title="Cordillera">cordillera</a> is, to a large extent, flanked by sedimentary layers from the <a href="/wiki/Cretaceous" title="Cretaceous">Cretaceous</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-183" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-183">&#91;183&#93;</a></sup> folded in an <a href="/wiki/Anticline" title="Anticline">anticline</a> structure. Between these orographic systems there are plains covered with tertiary and quaternary layers of gravel, sands and clayey <a href="/wiki/Marl" title="Marl">marls</a>. The depression contains lagoons and lakes, among which is that of <a href="/wiki/Maracaibo" title="Maracaibo">Maracaibo</a>, and presents, on the surface, <a href="/wiki/Alluvium" title="Alluvium">alluvial</a> deposits from the <a href="/wiki/Quaternary" title="Quaternary">Quaternary</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-184" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-184">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_Coastal_Range" title="Venezuelan Coastal Range">Coastal Mountain Range</a></li></ul>
<p>Also known as the Cordillera de la Costa, stretches along Venezuela's northern coast. This region is known for its lush tropical rainforests, stunning coastal views, and a rich variety of flora and fauna. The intermountain depressions, or valleys, between the mountain ranges are often home to fertile agricultural land and vibrant communities. These valleys offer a stark contrast to the rugged mountains that rise dramatically from the coast.
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Coro_region" title="Coro region">Lara-Falcón Highlands</a></li></ul>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:La_vegetaci%C3%B3n_m%C3%A1s_abundante_se%C3%B1ala_el_canal_de_los_r%C3%ADos.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/La_vegetaci%C3%B3n_m%C3%A1s_abundante_se%C3%B1ala_el_canal_de_los_r%C3%ADos.jpg/220px-La_vegetaci%C3%B3n_m%C3%A1s_abundante_se%C3%B1ala_el_canal_de_los_r%C3%ADos.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/La_vegetaci%C3%B3n_m%C3%A1s_abundante_se%C3%B1ala_el_canal_de_los_r%C3%ADos.jpg/330px-La_vegetaci%C3%B3n_m%C3%A1s_abundante_se%C3%B1ala_el_canal_de_los_r%C3%ADos.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/La_vegetaci%C3%B3n_m%C3%A1s_abundante_se%C3%B1ala_el_canal_de_los_r%C3%ADos.jpg/440px-La_vegetaci%C3%B3n_m%C3%A1s_abundante_se%C3%B1ala_el_canal_de_los_r%C3%ADos.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3648" data-file-height="2736" /></a><figcaption>Los Llanos, <a href="/wiki/Apure_state" class="mw-redirect" title="Apure state">Apure state</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Situated in northwestern Venezuela, the Lara-Falcón Highlands exhibit a terrain defined by plateaus and rolling hills. These highlands provide a significant contrast to the surrounding lowlands and coastal areas. The relief is characterized by gently sloping plateaus that support agriculture, including coffee and cacao cultivation. This region's semi-arid climate and picturesque landscapes make it an important agricultural and tourism center.
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Maracaibo_Basin" title="Maracaibo Basin">Lake Maracaibo Lowlands</a></li></ul>
<p>Encompass the basin of <a href="/wiki/Lake_Maracaibo" title="Lake Maracaibo">Lake Maracaibo</a> and the plains surrounding the <a href="/wiki/Gulf_of_Venezuela" title="Gulf of Venezuela">Gulf of Venezuela</a>. This region offers two distinct plains—the northern one is relatively dry, while the southern one is humid and dotted with swamps. The relief here is primarily characterized by flat terrain, with the exception of some elevated areas near the lake. Lake Maracaibo itself sits in a depression, surrounded by oil-rich lands and productive agricultural areas.<sup id="cite_ref-:4_179-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:4-179">&#91;179&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_Andes" title="Venezuelan Andes">The Andes</a></li></ul>
<p>The Venezuelan Andes, part of the broader <a href="/wiki/Andes" title="Andes">Andes</a> mountain range, offer a striking relief with towering peaks, deep valleys, and fertile intermontane basins. Dominated by these corpulent mountain ranges, including Venezuela's highest peak, <a href="/wiki/Bol%C3%ADvar_Peak" class="mw-redirect" title="Bolívar Peak">Bolívar Peak</a>, the region's rugged and picturesque landscapes are defined by its high-altitude terrain. The unique relief of this area finds its origins in the <a href="/wiki/Last_Glacial_Period" title="Last Glacial Period">Last Glacial Period</a>, where the interplay of repeated glacier advances and retreats sculpted the landscape, shaped by the cold, high-altitude climate. This glacial heritage has left a lasting imprint, with glaciers carving deep valleys and polishing rugged peaks, while sheltered intramontane valleys offer fertile soils and temperate microclimates, creating ideal conditions for agriculture and human settlement.
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_Llanos" title="Venezuelan Llanos">Los Llanos</a></li></ul>
<p>Los Llanos, or "the plains," are expansive sedimentary basins characterized by predominantly flat relief.<sup id="cite_ref-185" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-185">&#91;185&#93;</a></sup> However, the eastern Llanos feature low-plateaus and the Unare depression, created through mesa erosion, adding diversity to the terrain. This region is subject to seasonal flooding, transforming the flat plains into a vast wetland during the rainy season. The relief here influences the region's unique ecosystems, including extensive grasslands and abundant wildlife.
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Guayana_natural_region" title="Guayana natural region">Guiana Shield</a></li></ul>
<p>The Guiana Shield boasts a varied relief shaped by geological processes over millions of years. This region encompasses peneplains, rugged mountain ranges, foothills, and the iconic <a href="/wiki/Tepuis" class="mw-redirect" title="Tepuis">tepuis</a>, or table-top mountains. The tepuis stand as isolated, flat-topped plateaus that rise dramatically from the surrounding terrain. This unique relief contributes to the region's remarkable biodiversity and scientific significance.<sup id="cite_ref-:6_181-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:6-181">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Orinoco_Delta" title="Orinoco Delta">Orinoco Delta</a></li></ul><p>
The Orinoco Delta's relief is characterized by a complex system of lands and waters. It consists of numerous channels, islands, and shifting sedimentary deposits. While the relief may appear relatively uniform, it conceals a dynamic environment influenced by seasonal flooding and sediment deposition. This complex deltaic relief supports diverse aquatic life and the livelihoods of indigenous communities adapted to its ever-changing landscapes.<sup id="cite_ref-:5_180-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-180">&#91;180&#93;</a></sup></p><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Valle_de_Mifaf%C3%AD_2.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Valle_de_Mifaf%C3%AD_2.jpg/220px-Valle_de_Mifaf%C3%AD_2.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Valle_de_Mifaf%C3%AD_2.jpg/330px-Valle_de_Mifaf%C3%AD_2.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Valle_de_Mifaf%C3%AD_2.jpg/440px-Valle_de_Mifaf%C3%AD_2.jpg 2x" data-file-width="6016" data-file-height="4000" /></a><figcaption>Valle de Mifafí, <a href="/wiki/M%C3%A9rida_State" class="mw-redirect" title="Mérida State">Mérida State</a></figcaption></figure>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Valleys">Valleys</span></h3>
<p>The valleys are undoubtedly the most important type of <a href="/wiki/Landscape" title="Landscape">landscape</a> in the Venezuelan territory,<sup id="cite_ref-186" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-186">&#91;186&#93;</a></sup> not because of their spatial extension, but because they are the environment where most of the country's population and economic activities are concentrated. On the other hand, there are valleys throughout almost all the national space, except in the great sedimentary basins of the Llanos and the depression of the <a href="/wiki/Maracaibo_Lake" class="mw-redirect" title="Maracaibo Lake">Maracaibo Lake</a>, except also in the Amazonian peneplains.<sup id="cite_ref-:1_187-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-187">&#91;187&#93;</a></sup>
By their modeling, the valleys of the Venezuelan territory belong mainly to two types: valleys of <a href="/wiki/Fluvial" class="mw-redirect" title="Fluvial">fluvial</a> type and valleys of <a href="/wiki/Glacial" class="mw-redirect" title="Glacial">glacial</a> type.<sup id="cite_ref-188" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-188">&#91;188&#93;</a></sup> Much more frequent, the former largely dominate the latter, which are restricted to the highest parts of the Andes. Moreover, most glacial valleys are relics of a past geologic epoch, which culminated some 10,000 to 12,000 years ago.
</p>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Venezuela_-_Caracas_-_Mirador_de_Valle_Arriba.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/Venezuela_-_Caracas_-_Mirador_de_Valle_Arriba.jpg/216px-Venezuela_-_Caracas_-_Mirador_de_Valle_Arriba.jpg" decoding="async" width="216" height="154" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/Venezuela_-_Caracas_-_Mirador_de_Valle_Arriba.jpg/324px-Venezuela_-_Caracas_-_Mirador_de_Valle_Arriba.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/Venezuela_-_Caracas_-_Mirador_de_Valle_Arriba.jpg/432px-Venezuela_-_Caracas_-_Mirador_de_Valle_Arriba.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3734" data-file-height="2655" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Caracas" title="Caracas">Caracas</a> Valley</figcaption></figure>
<p>The deep and narrow Andean valleys are very different from the wide depressions of <a href="/wiki/Aragua" title="Aragua">Aragua</a> and Carabobo, in the <a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_Coastal_Range" title="Venezuelan Coastal Range">Cordillera de la Costa</a>, or from the valleys nestled in the Mesas de <a href="/wiki/Monagas" title="Monagas">Monagas</a>. These examples indicate that the configuration of the local relief is decisive in identifying regional types of valleys. Likewise, due to their warm climate, the Guayana valleys are distinguished from the temperate or cold <a href="/wiki/Andes" title="Andes">Andean valleys</a> by their humid environment. Both are, in turn, different from the semi-arid depressions of the states of Lara and Falcón.
</p><p>The Andean valleys, essentially agricultural, precociously populated but nowadays in loss of speed, do not confront the same problems of space occupation as the strongly urbanized and industrialized valleys of the central section of the Cordillera de la Costa. On the other hand, the unpopulated and practically untouched <a href="/wiki/The_Guianas" title="The Guianas">Guiana</a> valleys are another category this area is called the Lost World (<i>Mundo Perdido</i>).<sup id="cite_ref-:1_187-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-187">&#91;187&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The Andean valleys are undoubtedly the most impressive of the Venezuelan territory because of the energy of the encasing reliefs, whose summits often dominate the valley bottoms by 3,000 to 3,500 <a href="/wiki/Meters" class="mw-redirect" title="Meters">meters</a> of relative <a href="/wiki/Altitude" title="Altitude">altitude</a>. They are also the most picturesque in terms of their style of habitat, forms of land use, <a href="/wiki/Handicraft" title="Handicraft">handicraft</a> production and all the traditions linked to these activities. these activities<sup id="cite_ref-:1_187-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-187">&#91;187&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Deserts">Deserts</span></h3>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Medanos_de_Coro_Falcon.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f0/Medanos_de_Coro_Falcon.jpg/211px-Medanos_de_Coro_Falcon.jpg" decoding="async" width="211" height="158" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f0/Medanos_de_Coro_Falcon.jpg/317px-Medanos_de_Coro_Falcon.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f0/Medanos_de_Coro_Falcon.jpg/422px-Medanos_de_Coro_Falcon.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2048" data-file-height="1536" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/M%C3%A9danos_de_Coro_National_Park" title="Médanos de Coro National Park">Médanos de Coro National Park</a>, <a href="/wiki/Paraguan%C3%A1_Peninsula" title="Paraguaná Peninsula">Paraguaná Peninsula</a>, <a href="/wiki/Falc%C3%B3n" title="Falcón">Falcón State</a>, Venezuela.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Venezuela has a great diversity of landscapes and climates,<sup id="cite_ref-189" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-189">&#91;189&#93;</a></sup> including arid and dry areas. The main <a href="/wiki/Desert" title="Desert">desert</a> in the country is in the state of Falcon near the city of Coro. It is now a protected park, the <a href="/wiki/M%C3%A9danos_de_Coro_National_Park" title="Médanos de Coro National Park">Médanos de Coro National Park</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-190" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-190">&#91;190&#93;</a></sup> The park is the largest of its kind in Venezuela, covering 91 square kilometres. The landscape is dotted with cacti and other xerophytic plants that can survive in humidity-free conditions near the desert.
</p><p>Desert wildlife includes mostly lizards, <a href="/wiki/Iguanas" class="mw-redirect" title="Iguanas">iguanas</a> and other reptiles. Although less frequent, the desert is home to some foxes, giant anteaters and rabbits. There are also some native bird populations, such as the sparrowhawk, tropical mockingbird, scaly dove and crested quail.
</p><p>Other desert areas in the country include part of the Guajira Desert in the Guajira Municipality in the north of Zulia State<sup id="cite_ref-191" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-191">&#91;191&#93;</a></sup> and facing the <a href="/wiki/Gulf_of_Venezuela" title="Gulf of Venezuela">Gulf of Venezuela</a>, the Médanos de Capanaparo<sup id="cite_ref-192" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-192">&#91;192&#93;</a></sup> in the Santos Luzardo National Park in <a href="/wiki/Apure_State" class="mw-redirect" title="Apure State">Apure State</a>, the Medanos de la Isla de Zapara<sup id="cite_ref-193" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-193">&#91;193&#93;</a></sup> in Zulia State, the so-called Hundición de Yay<sup id="cite_ref-194" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-194">&#91;194&#93;</a></sup> in the Andrés Eloy Blanco Municipality of Lara State, and the Urumaco Formation also in Falcón State.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Government_and_politics">Government and politics</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Venezuela" title="Government of Venezuela">Government of Venezuela</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cabinet_of_Venezuela" title="Cabinet of Venezuela">Cabinet of Venezuela</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Politics_of_Venezuela" title="Politics of Venezuela">Politics of Venezuela</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:LegislativoCentro.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/LegislativoCentro.jpg/220px-LegislativoCentro.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/LegislativoCentro.jpg/330px-LegislativoCentro.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/LegislativoCentro.jpg/440px-LegislativoCentro.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3872" data-file-height="2592" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/National_Assembly_of_Venezuela" class="mw-redirect" title="National Assembly of Venezuela">National Assembly of Venezuela</a> <a href="/wiki/Palacio_Federal_Legislativo" title="Palacio Federal Legislativo">building</a></figcaption></figure>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Residencia_presidencial_La_Casona,_Caracas.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Residencia_presidencial_La_Casona%2C_Caracas.jpg/241px-Residencia_presidencial_La_Casona%2C_Caracas.jpg" decoding="async" width="241" height="172" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Residencia_presidencial_La_Casona%2C_Caracas.jpg/362px-Residencia_presidencial_La_Casona%2C_Caracas.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Residencia_presidencial_La_Casona%2C_Caracas.jpg/482px-Residencia_presidencial_La_Casona%2C_Caracas.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4032" data-file-height="2880" /></a><figcaption>La Casona presidential residence in Caracas, now a <a href="/wiki/Museum" title="Museum">museum</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Two major blocs of <a href="/wiki/List_of_political_parties_in_Venezuela" title="List of political parties in Venezuela">political parties</a> are in Venezuela: the incumbent leftist bloc United Socialist Party of Venezuela (PSUV), its major allies <a href="/wiki/Fatherland_for_All" title="Fatherland for All">Fatherland for All</a> (PPT) and the Communist Party of Venezuela (PCV), and the opposition bloc grouped into the electoral coalition <a href="/wiki/Mesa_de_la_Unidad_Democr%C3%A1tica" class="mw-redirect" title="Mesa de la Unidad Democrática">Mesa de la Unidad Democrática</a>. This includes <a href="/wiki/A_New_Era" title="A New Era">A New Era</a> (UNT) together with allied parties <a href="/wiki/Project_Venezuela" title="Project Venezuela">Project Venezuela</a>, <a href="/wiki/Justice_First" title="Justice First">Justice First</a>, <a href="/wiki/Movement_for_Socialism_(Venezuela)" class="mw-redirect" title="Movement for Socialism (Venezuela)">Movement for Socialism</a> (MAS) and others.
</p><p>The Venezuelan president is elected by a vote, with direct and <a href="/wiki/Universal_suffrage" title="Universal suffrage">universal suffrage</a>, and is both <a href="/wiki/Head_of_state" title="Head of state">head of state</a> and <a href="/wiki/Head_of_government" title="Head of government">head of government</a>. The term of office is six years, and (as of 15 February 2009) a president may be re-elected an unlimited number of times. The president appoints the vice president and decides the size and composition of the cabinet and makes appointments to it with the involvement of the legislature. The president can ask the legislature to reconsider portions of laws he finds objectionable, but a simple parliamentary majority can override these objections.
</p><p>The president may ask the National Assembly to pass an <a href="/wiki/Enabling_act#In_Venezuela" title="Enabling act">enabling act</a> granting the ability to <a href="/wiki/Rule_by_decree" title="Rule by decree">rule by decree</a> in specified policy areas; this requires a two-thirds majority in the Assembly. Since 1959, six Venezuelan presidents have been granted such powers.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Unicameral" class="mw-redirect" title="Unicameral">unicameral</a> Venezuelan parliament is the <i>Asamblea Nacional</i> ("National Assembly"). The number of members is variable – each state and the Capital district elect three representatives plus the result of dividing the state population by 1.1% of the total population of the country.<sup id="cite_ref-195" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-195">&#91;195&#93;</a></sup> Three seats are reserved for representatives of Venezuela's indigenous peoples. For the 2011–2016 period the number of seats is 165.<sup id="cite_ref-196" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-196">&#91;196&#93;</a></sup> All deputies serve five-year terms.
</p><p>The voting age in Venezuela is 18. Voting is not <a href="/wiki/Compulsory_voting" title="Compulsory voting">compulsory</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-TG_197-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TG-197">&#91;197&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Law_of_Venezuela" title="Law of Venezuela">legal system of Venezuela</a> belongs to the <a href="/wiki/Civil_law_(legal_system)" title="Civil law (legal system)">Continental Law</a> tradition. The highest <a href="/wiki/Judiciary" title="Judiciary">judicial</a> body is the <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Tribunal_of_Justice_(Venezuela)" title="Supreme Tribunal of Justice (Venezuela)">Supreme Tribunal of Justice</a> or <i>Tribunal Supremo de Justicia</i>, whose magistrates are elected by parliament for a single two-year term. The <a href="/wiki/National_Electoral_Council_(Venezuela)" title="National Electoral Council (Venezuela)">National Electoral Council</a> (<i>Consejo Nacional Electoral</i>, or <i>CNE</i>) is in charge of electoral processes; it is formed by five main directors elected by the National Assembly. Supreme Court president Luisa Estela Morales said in December 2009 that Venezuela had moved away from "a rigid division of powers" toward a system characterized by "intense coordination" between the branches of government. Morales clarified that each power must be independent.<sup id="cite_ref-198" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-198">&#91;198&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Suspension_of_constitutional_rights">Suspension of constitutional rights</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Venezuela_protests_against_the_Nicolas_Maduro_government,_Altamira_Square_6.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Venezuela_protests_against_the_Nicolas_Maduro_government%2C_Altamira_Square_6.JPG/220px-Venezuela_protests_against_the_Nicolas_Maduro_government%2C_Altamira_Square_6.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Venezuela_protests_against_the_Nicolas_Maduro_government%2C_Altamira_Square_6.JPG/330px-Venezuela_protests_against_the_Nicolas_Maduro_government%2C_Altamira_Square_6.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Venezuela_protests_against_the_Nicolas_Maduro_government%2C_Altamira_Square_6.JPG/440px-Venezuela_protests_against_the_Nicolas_Maduro_government%2C_Altamira_Square_6.JPG 2x" data-file-width="4288" data-file-height="3216" /></a><figcaption>Protests in <a href="/wiki/Altamira_(Caracas)" class="mw-redirect" title="Altamira (Caracas)">Altamira</a>, Caracas (2014)</figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/2015_Venezuelan_parliamentary_election" title="2015 Venezuelan parliamentary election">2015 parliamentary elections</a> were held on 6 December 2015 to elect the 164 <a href="/wiki/Deputies" class="mw-redirect" title="Deputies">deputies</a> and three indigenous representatives of the National Assembly. In 2014, a series of protest and demonstrations began in Venezuela, attributed<sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Words_to_watch#Unsupported_attributions" title="Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch"><span title="The material near this tag may use weasel words or too-vague attribution. (May 2019)">by whom?</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> to inflation, violence and shortages in Venezuela. The protests were largely peaceful.<sup id="cite_ref-SVCOprotestINFO_199-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-SVCOprotestINFO-199">&#91;199&#93;</a></sup>
The government has accused the protest of being motivated by <a href="/wiki/Fascists" class="mw-redirect" title="Fascists">fascists</a>, opposition leaders, capitalism and foreign influence,<sup id="cite_ref-Milne_200-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Milne-200">&#91;200&#93;</a></sup> 
President Maduro acknowledged <a href="/wiki/PSUV" class="mw-redirect" title="PSUV">PSUV</a> defeat, but attributed the opposition's victory to an intensification of an economic war. Despite this, Maduro said "I will stop by hook or by crook the opposition coming to power, whatever the costs, in any way".<sup id="cite_ref-201" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-201">&#91;201&#93;</a></sup> In the following months, Maduro fulfilled his promise of preventing the elected National Assembly from legislating. The first steps taken by PSUV and government were the substitution of the entire <a href="/wiki/Supreme_court" title="Supreme court">Supreme court</a> a day after the Parliamentary Elections<sup id="cite_ref-prodavinci.com_202-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-prodavinci.com-202">&#91;202&#93;</a></sup> contrary to the Constitution of Venezuela, acclaimed as a fraud by the majority of the Venezuelan and international press.<sup id="cite_ref-larazon.net_203-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-larazon.net-203">&#91;203&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-el-nacional.com_204-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-el-nacional.com-204">&#91;204&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-bbc.com_205-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bbc.com-205">&#91;205&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ntn24web.com_206-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ntn24web.com-206">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup> The <i>Financial Times</i> described the function of the Supreme Court in Venezuela as "rubber stamping executive whims and vetoing legislation".<sup id="cite_ref-:0_207-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-207">&#91;207&#93;</a></sup> The PSUV government used this violation to suspend several elected opponents.<sup id="cite_ref-208" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-208">&#91;208&#93;</a></sup> Maduro said that "the Amnesty law (approved by the Parliament) will not be executed" and asked the Supreme Court to declare it unconstitutional.<sup id="cite_ref-209" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-209">&#91;209&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 16 January 2016, Maduro approved an unconstitutional economic emergency decree,<sup id="cite_ref-210" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-210">&#91;210&#93;</a></sup> relegating to his own figure the legislative and executive powers, while also holding judiciary power through the fraudulent designation of judges the day after the election on 6 December 2015.<sup id="cite_ref-prodavinci.com_202-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-prodavinci.com-202">&#91;202&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-larazon.net_203-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-larazon.net-203">&#91;203&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-el-nacional.com_204-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-el-nacional.com-204">&#91;204&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-bbc.com_205-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bbc.com-205">&#91;205&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ntn24web.com_206-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ntn24web.com-206">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup> From these events, Maduro effectively controls all three branches of government. On 14 May 2016, constitutional guarantees were in fact suspended when Maduro decreed the extension of the economic emergency decree for another 60 days and declared a State of Emergency,<sup id="cite_ref-211" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-211">&#91;211&#93;</a></sup> which is a clear violation of the <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Venezuela" title="Constitution of Venezuela">Constitution of Venezuela</a><sup id="cite_ref-212" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-212">&#91;212&#93;</a></sup> in the Article 338th: "The approval of the extension of States of emergency corresponds to the National Assembly." Thus, constitutional rights in Venezuela are considered suspended in fact by many publications<sup id="cite_ref-213" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-213">&#91;213&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-214" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-214">&#91;214&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-215" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-215">&#91;215&#93;</a></sup> and public figures.<sup id="cite_ref-216" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-216">&#91;216&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-217" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-217">&#91;217&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-218" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-218">&#91;218&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 14 May 2016, the <a href="/wiki/Organization_of_American_States" title="Organization of American States">Organization of American States</a> was considering the application of the <a href="/wiki/Inter-American_Democratic_Charter" title="Inter-American Democratic Charter">Inter-American Democratic Charter</a><sup id="cite_ref-219" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-219">&#91;219&#93;</a></sup> sanctions for non-compliance to its own constitution.
</p><p>In March 2017, the Venezuelan Supreme Court took over law making powers from the National Assembly<sup id="cite_ref-220" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-220">&#91;220&#93;</a></sup> but reversed its decision the following day.<sup id="cite_ref-221" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-221">&#91;221&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Foreign_relations">Foreign relations</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Venezuela" title="Foreign relations of Venezuela">Foreign relations of Venezuela</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Guayana_Esequiba_(zona_completa).png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Guayana_Esequiba_%28zona_completa%29.png/220px-Guayana_Esequiba_%28zona_completa%29.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="221" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Guayana_Esequiba_%28zona_completa%29.png/330px-Guayana_Esequiba_%28zona_completa%29.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Guayana_Esequiba_%28zona_completa%29.png/440px-Guayana_Esequiba_%28zona_completa%29.png 2x" data-file-width="784" data-file-height="786" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Guayana_Esequiba" title="Guayana Esequiba">Guayana Esequiba</a> claim area is a territory administered by <a href="/wiki/Guyana" title="Guyana">Guyana</a> and historically claimed by Venezuela.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Throughout most of the 20th century, Venezuela maintained friendly relations with most Latin American and Western nations. Relations between Venezuela and the United States government worsened in 2002, after the 2002 Venezuelan coup d'état attempt during which the U.S. government recognized the short-lived interim presidency of <a href="/wiki/Pedro_Carmona" title="Pedro Carmona">Pedro Carmona</a>. In 2015, Venezuela was declared a national security threat by U.S. president <a href="/wiki/Barack_Obama" title="Barack Obama">Barack Obama</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-222" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-222">&#91;222&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-223" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-223">&#91;223&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-224" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-224">&#91;224&#93;</a></sup> Correspondingly, ties to various Latin American and <a href="/wiki/Middle_East" title="Middle East">Middle Eastern</a> countries not allied to the U.S. have strengthened.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (March 2023)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p><p>Venezuela seeks alternative <a href="/wiki/Western_Hemisphere" title="Western Hemisphere">hemispheric</a> integration via such proposals as the <a href="/wiki/Bolivarian_Alternative_for_the_Americas" class="mw-redirect" title="Bolivarian Alternative for the Americas">Bolivarian Alternative for the Americas</a> trade proposal and the newly launched Latin American television network <a href="/wiki/TeleSUR" class="mw-redirect" title="TeleSUR">teleSUR</a>. Venezuela is one of five nations in the world—along with Russia, Nicaragua, Nauru, and Syria—to have recognized the independence of <a href="/wiki/International_recognition_of_Abkhazia_and_South_Ossetia" title="International recognition of Abkhazia and South Ossetia">Abkhazia and South Ossetia</a>. Venezuela was a proponent of <a href="/wiki/Organization_of_American_States" title="Organization of American States">OAS</a>'s decision to adopt its Anti-Corruption Convention<sup id="cite_ref-225" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-225">&#91;225&#93;</a></sup> and is actively working in the <a href="/wiki/Mercosur" title="Mercosur">Mercosur</a> trade bloc to push increased trade and energy integration. Globally, it seeks a "<a href="/wiki/Polarity_in_international_relations" class="mw-redirect" title="Polarity in international relations">multi-polar</a>" world based on strengthened ties among undeveloped countries.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (March 2023)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:XIV_cumbre_del_ALBA-TCP.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/XIV_cumbre_del_ALBA-TCP.jpg/220px-XIV_cumbre_del_ALBA-TCP.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="148" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/XIV_cumbre_del_ALBA-TCP.jpg/330px-XIV_cumbre_del_ALBA-TCP.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/XIV_cumbre_del_ALBA-TCP.jpg/440px-XIV_cumbre_del_ALBA-TCP.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5939" data-file-height="3989" /></a><figcaption>President Maduro among other Latin American leaders participating in a 2017 <a href="/wiki/ALBA" title="ALBA">ALBA</a> gathering</figcaption></figure>
<p>On 26 April 2017, Venezuela announced its intention to withdraw from the OAS.<sup id="cite_ref-226" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-226">&#91;226&#93;</a></sup> Venezuelan Foreign Minister <a href="/wiki/Delcy_Rodr%C3%ADguez" title="Delcy Rodríguez">Delcy Rodríguez</a> said that President <a href="/wiki/Nicol%C3%A1s_Maduro" title="Nicolás Maduro">Nicolás Maduro</a> plans to publicly renounce Venezuela's membership on 27 April 2017. It will take two years for the country to formally leave. During this period, the country does not plan on participating in the OAS.<sup id="cite_ref-227" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-227">&#91;227&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Venezuela is involved in a long-standing disagreement about the control of the <a href="/wiki/Guayana_Esequiba" title="Guayana Esequiba">Guayana Esequiba</a> area.
</p><p>Venezuela may suffer a deterioration of its power in international affairs if the global <a href="/wiki/Energy_transition" title="Energy transition">transition to renewable energy</a> is completed. It is ranked 151 out of 156 countries in the index of Geopolitical Gains and Losses after energy transition (GeGaLo).<sup id="cite_ref-228" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-228">&#91;228&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Military">Military</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/National_Bolivarian_Armed_Forces_of_Venezuela" title="National Bolivarian Armed Forces of Venezuela">National Bolivarian Armed Forces of Venezuela</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Venezuelan_Air_Force_Sukhoi_SU-30MK2_AADPR-2.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Venezuelan_Air_Force_Sukhoi_SU-30MK2_AADPR-2.jpg/220px-Venezuelan_Air_Force_Sukhoi_SU-30MK2_AADPR-2.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="155" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Venezuelan_Air_Force_Sukhoi_SU-30MK2_AADPR-2.jpg/330px-Venezuelan_Air_Force_Sukhoi_SU-30MK2_AADPR-2.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Venezuelan_Air_Force_Sukhoi_SU-30MK2_AADPR-2.jpg/440px-Venezuelan_Air_Force_Sukhoi_SU-30MK2_AADPR-2.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1024" data-file-height="721" /></a><figcaption>A <a href="/wiki/Sukhoi_Su-30" title="Sukhoi Su-30">Sukhoi Su-30</a>MKV of the Venezuelan Air Force</figcaption></figure>
<p>The Bolivarian National Armed Forces of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela (Fuerza Armada Nacional Bolivariana, FANB) are the overall unified military forces of Venezuela.
