<div class="thumbcaption">
<p>Religion in Venezuela (2011)<sup id="cite_ref-grumilla_342-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-grumilla-342">&#91;342&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r981673959">.mw-parser-output .legend{page-break-inside:avoid;break-inside:avoid-column}.mw-parser-output .legend-color{display:inline-block;min-width:1.25em;height:1.25em;line-height:1.25;margin:1px 0;text-align:center;border:1px solid black;background-color:transparent;color:black}.mw-parser-output .legend-text{}</style><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:Blue; color:white;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Roman_Catholicism" class="mw-redirect" title="Roman Catholicism">Catholic</a> (71%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:DodgerBlue; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Protestant" class="mw-redirect" title="Protestant">Protestant</a> (17%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:LightGray; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Irreligion" title="Irreligion">No religion</a> (7%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:yellow; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;Other religion (3%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:white; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;No answer (1%)</div>
</div>
</div></div>
<p>According to a 2011 poll, 88% of the population is Christian, primarily <a href="/wiki/Roman_Catholic" class="mw-redirect" title="Roman Catholic">Roman Catholic</a> (71%), and the remaining 17% <a href="/wiki/Protestant" class="mw-redirect" title="Protestant">Protestant</a>, primarily <a href="/wiki/Evangelicals" class="mw-redirect" title="Evangelicals">Evangelicals</a> (in Latin America Protestants are usually called <i>"evangélicos"</i>). 8% of Venezuelans are irreligious. Almost 3% of the population follow another religion (1% of these people practice <a href="/wiki/Santer%C3%ADa" title="Santería">Santería</a>).<sup id="cite_ref-grumilla_342-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-grumilla-342">&#91;342&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>There are small but influential <a href="/wiki/Muslim" class="mw-redirect" title="Muslim">Muslim</a>, <a href="/wiki/Druze" title="Druze">Druze</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Khalifa_2013_loc=6-7_343-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Khalifa_2013_loc=6-7-343">&#91;343&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-344" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-344">&#91;344&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Buddhist" class="mw-redirect" title="Buddhist">Buddhist</a>, and Jewish communities. The Muslim community of more than 100,000 is concentrated among persons of <a href="/wiki/Lebanese_people" title="Lebanese people">Lebanese</a> and <a href="/wiki/Syrian_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Syrian people">Syrian</a> descent living in <a href="/wiki/Nueva_Esparta" title="Nueva Esparta">Nueva Esparta</a> state, <a href="/wiki/Punto_Fijo" title="Punto Fijo">Punto Fijo</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Caracas" title="Caracas">Caracas</a> area. Venezuela is home of the largest Druze communities outside the Middle East,<sup id="cite_ref-Los_Angeles_Times_345-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Los_Angeles_Times-345">&#91;345&#93;</a></sup> the <a href="/wiki/Druze" title="Druze">Druze</a> community are estimated around 60,000,<sup id="cite_ref-Los_Angeles_Times_345-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Los_Angeles_Times-345">&#91;345&#93;</a></sup> and concentrated among persons of <a href="/wiki/Lebanese_people" title="Lebanese people">Lebanese</a> and <a href="/wiki/Syrian_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Syrian people">Syrian</a> descent.<sup id="cite_ref-346" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-346">&#91;346&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Khalifa_2013_loc=6-7_343-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Khalifa_2013_loc=6-7-343">&#91;343&#93;</a></sup> Buddhism is practiced by over 52,000 people. The Buddhist community is made up mainly of Chinese, Japanese, and Korean people.
</p><p>The Jewish community has shrunk in recent years due to rising economic pressures and <a href="/wiki/Antisemitism_in_Venezuela" title="Antisemitism in Venezuela">antisemitism in Venezuela</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Hurricane_347-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hurricane-347">&#91;347&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-SRI_348-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-SRI-348">&#91;348&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-349" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-349">&#91;349&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-350" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-350">&#91;350&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-351" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-351">&#91;351&#93;</a></sup> with the population declining from 22,000 in 1999<sup id="cite_ref-TOERaid_352-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TOERaid-352">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup> to less than 7,000 in 2015.<sup id="cite_ref-AJjan2015_353-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AJjan2015-353">&#91;353&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Health">Health</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Health_care_in_Venezuela" title="Health care in Venezuela">Health care in Venezuela</a> and <a href="/wiki/Mission_Barrio_Adentro" title="Mission Barrio Adentro">Mission Barrio Adentro</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Hospital_Universitario-UCV.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Hospital_Universitario-UCV.JPG/220px-Hospital_Universitario-UCV.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="293" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Hospital_Universitario-UCV.JPG/330px-Hospital_Universitario-UCV.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Hospital_Universitario-UCV.JPG/440px-Hospital_Universitario-UCV.JPG 2x" data-file-width="1536" data-file-height="2048" /></a><figcaption>University Hospital, <a href="/wiki/Central_University_of_Venezuela" title="Central University of Venezuela">Central University of Venezuela</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Venezuela has a national <a href="/wiki/Universal_health_care" title="Universal health care">universal health care</a> system. The current government has created a program to expand access to health care known as <a href="/wiki/Mission_Barrio_Adentro" title="Mission Barrio Adentro">Misión Barrio Adentro</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Venezuela_Information_Office_354-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Venezuela_Information_Office-354">&#91;354&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-355" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-355">&#91;355&#93;</a></sup> although its efficiency and work conditions have been criticized.<sup id="cite_ref-MBAeu_356-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MBAeu-356">&#91;356&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-357" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-357">&#91;357&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ABCnov2014_358-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ABCnov2014-358">&#91;358&#93;</a></sup> As of December 2014 an estimated 80% of Barrio Adentro establishments in Venezuela are abandoned.<sup id="cite_ref-359" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-359">&#91;359&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-LPdec2014_360-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-LPdec2014-360">&#91;360&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Infant_mortality" title="Infant mortality">Infant mortality</a> in Venezuela was 19 deaths per 1,000 births for 2014 which was lower than the South American average (To compare: The U.S. figure was 6 deaths per 1,000 births in 2013).<sup id="cite_ref-ciawfb_57-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ciawfb-57">&#91;57&#93;</a></sup> Child <a href="/wiki/Malnutrition" title="Malnutrition">malnutrition</a> was 17%. <a href="/wiki/Delta_Amacuro" title="Delta Amacuro">Delta Amacuro</a> and <a href="/wiki/Amazonas_(Venezuelan_state)" title="Amazonas (Venezuelan state)">Amazonas</a> had the nation's highest rates.<sup id="cite_ref-361" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-361">&#91;361&#93;</a></sup> According to the United Nations, 32% of Venezuelans lacked adequate sanitation, primarily those living in rural areas.<sup id="cite_ref-362" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-362">&#91;362&#93;</a></sup> Diseases ranging from <a href="/wiki/Diphtheria" title="Diphtheria">diphtheria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Plague_(disease)" title="Plague (disease)">plague</a>, <a href="/wiki/Malaria" title="Malaria">malaria</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Finnegan_244-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Finnegan-244">&#91;244&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Typhoid" class="mw-redirect" title="Typhoid">typhoid</a> fever, <a href="/wiki/Yellow_fever" title="Yellow fever">yellow fever</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cholera" title="Cholera">cholera</a>, <a href="/wiki/Hepatitis_A" title="Hepatitis A">hepatitis A</a>, <a href="/wiki/Hepatitis_B" title="Hepatitis B">hepatitis B</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Hepatitis_D" title="Hepatitis D">hepatitis D</a> were present in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-guardian1_363-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guardian1-363">&#91;363&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Obesity" title="Obesity">Obesity</a> was prevalent in approximately 30% of the adult population.<sup id="cite_ref-ciawfb_57-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ciawfb-57">&#91;57&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Venezuela had a total of 150 <a href="/wiki/Water_supply_and_sanitation_in_Venezuela" title="Water supply and sanitation in Venezuela">sewage treatment plants</a>; 13% of the population lacked access to drinking water, but this number had been dropping.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChávez2004_364-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChávez2004-364">&#91;364&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template noprint Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:No_original_research#Primary,_secondary_and_tertiary_sources" title="Wikipedia:No original research"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable secondary sources. (October 2022)">non-primary source needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p><p>During the economic crisis observed under President Maduro's presidency, medical professionals were forced to perform outdated treatments on patients.<sup id="cite_ref-365" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-365">&#91;365&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Education">Education</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Education_in_Venezuela" title="Education in Venezuela">Education in Venezuela</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Illiteracy_in_Venezuela.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Illiteracy_in_Venezuela.svg/220px-Illiteracy_in_Venezuela.svg.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="181" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Illiteracy_in_Venezuela.svg/330px-Illiteracy_in_Venezuela.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Illiteracy_in_Venezuela.svg/440px-Illiteracy_in_Venezuela.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="443" data-file-height="365" /></a><figcaption>Illiteracy rate in Venezuela based on data from UNESCO<sup id="cite_ref-unesco1988_366-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-unesco1988-366">&#91;366&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-unesco-uis_367-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-unesco-uis-367">&#91;367&#93;</a></sup> and the Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE) of Venezuela<sup id="cite_ref-ortega_368-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ortega-368">&#91;368&#93;</a></sup></figcaption></figure>
<p>In 2008, 95.2% of the adult population was literate.<sup id="cite_ref-hdrstats.undp.org_369-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hdrstats.undp.org-369">&#91;369&#93;</a></sup> The net primary school enrollment rate was at 91% and the net secondary school enrollment rate was at 63% in 2005.<sup id="cite_ref-hdrstats.undp.org_369-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hdrstats.undp.org-369">&#91;369&#93;</a></sup> Venezuela has a number of universities, of which the most prestigious are the <a href="/wiki/Central_University_of_Venezuela" title="Central University of Venezuela">Central University of Venezuela</a> founded in 1721, the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Zulia" title="University of Zulia">University of Zulia</a>, the <a href="/wiki/University_of_the_Andes_(Venezuela)" title="University of the Andes (Venezuela)">University of the Andes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sim%C3%B3n_Bol%C3%ADvar_University_(Venezuela)" title="Simón Bolívar University (Venezuela)">Simón Bolívar University</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Universidad_de_Oriente" title="Universidad de Oriente">University of the East</a>.
</p><p>Currently, many Venezuelan graduates seek a future abroad because of the country's troubled economy and heavy crime rate. Over 1.35 million Venezuelan college graduates have left the country since the beginning of the <a href="/wiki/Bolivarian_Revolution" title="Bolivarian Revolution">Bolivarian Revolution</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-ENHaug28_319-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ENHaug28-319">&#91;319&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Elimpulso23AUG_320-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Elimpulso23AUG-320">&#91;320&#93;</a></sup> It is believed that nearly 12% of Venezuelans live abroad, with Ireland becoming a popular destination for students.<sup id="cite_ref-370" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-370">&#91;370&#93;</a></sup> According to Claudio Bifano, president of the Venezuelan Academy of Physical, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences, more than half of all medical graduates had left Venezuela in 2013.<sup id="cite_ref-371" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-371">&#91;371&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>By 2018, over half of all Venezuelan children had <a href="/wiki/Dropped_out" class="mw-redirect" title="Dropped out">dropped out</a> of school, with 58% of students quitting nationwide while areas near bordering countries saw more than 80% of their students leave.<sup id="cite_ref-372" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-372">&#91;372&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:2_373-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-373">&#91;373&#93;</a></sup> Nationwide, about 93% of schools do not meet the minimum requirements to operate and 77% do not have utilities such as food, water or electricity.<sup id="cite_ref-:2_373-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-373">&#91;373&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Culture">Culture</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Culture_of_Venezuela" title="Culture of Venezuela">Culture of Venezuela</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Joropo_foto.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/Joropo_foto.jpg/220px-Joropo_foto.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="211" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/Joropo_foto.jpg/330px-Joropo_foto.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5e/Joropo_foto.jpg 2x" data-file-width="365" data-file-height="350" /></a><figcaption>The <i>joropo</i>, as depicted in a 1912 drawing by <a href="/wiki/Eloy_Palacios" title="Eloy Palacios">Eloy Palacios</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The culture of Venezuela is a melting pot made up of three main groups: The Indigenous Venezuelans, the Africans, and the Spanish.
</p><p>The Africans brought in many musical influences, especially introduction of the drum. The Spanish influence predominantes due to the colonization process and the socioeconomic structure it created. Spanish influences can be seen in the country's architecture, music, religion, and language.
</p><p>Venezuela was also enriched by immigration streams of Indian and European origin in the 19th century, especially from France. Most recently, immigration from the United States, Spain, Italy, and Portugal has enriched the already complex cultural mosaic.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (October 2020)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Petroglifos_en_Vigirima.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Petroglifos_en_Vigirima.jpg/259px-Petroglifos_en_Vigirima.jpg" decoding="async" width="259" height="194" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Petroglifos_en_Vigirima.jpg/389px-Petroglifos_en_Vigirima.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Petroglifos_en_Vigirima.jpg/518px-Petroglifos_en_Vigirima.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3648" data-file-height="2736" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Petroglyphs" class="mw-redirect" title="Petroglyphs">Petroglyphs</a> at Vigirima, <a href="/wiki/Carabobo_state" class="mw-redirect" title="Carabobo state">Carabobo state</a></figcaption></figure>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Architecture">Architecture</span></h3>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Casco_Central_Santa_Ana_de_Coro,_estado_Falcon,_Venezuela.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/Casco_Central_Santa_Ana_de_Coro%2C_estado_Falcon%2C_Venezuela.jpg/243px-Casco_Central_Santa_Ana_de_Coro%2C_estado_Falcon%2C_Venezuela.jpg" decoding="async" width="243" height="162" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/Casco_Central_Santa_Ana_de_Coro%2C_estado_Falcon%2C_Venezuela.jpg/365px-Casco_Central_Santa_Ana_de_Coro%2C_estado_Falcon%2C_Venezuela.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/Casco_Central_Santa_Ana_de_Coro%2C_estado_Falcon%2C_Venezuela.jpg/486px-Casco_Central_Santa_Ana_de_Coro%2C_estado_Falcon%2C_Venezuela.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3504" data-file-height="2336" /></a><figcaption>The historic center of Coro, a <a href="/wiki/World_Heritage_Sites_by_country" title="World Heritage Sites by country">World Heritage Site</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-374" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-374">&#91;374&#93;</a></sup> is an example of <a href="/wiki/Spanish_Colonial_architecture" title="Spanish Colonial architecture">Spanish colonial architecture</a> in Venezuela.</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Carlos_Ra%C3%BAl_Villanueva" title="Carlos Raúl Villanueva">Carlos Raúl Villanueva</a><sup id="cite_ref-375" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-375">&#91;375&#93;</a></sup> was the most important Venezuelan architect of the modern era; he designed the Central University of Venezuela, (a <a href="/wiki/World_Heritage_Site" title="World Heritage Site">World Heritage Site</a>) and its Aula Magna. Other notable architectural works include the Capitolio, the <a href="/wiki/Baralt_Theatre" title="Baralt Theatre">Baralt Theatre</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Teresa_Carre%C3%B1o_Cultural_Complex" title="Teresa Carreño Cultural Complex">Teresa Carreño Cultural Complex</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/General_Rafael_Urdaneta_Bridge" title="General Rafael Urdaneta Bridge">General Rafael Urdaneta Bridge</a>.
In Venezuela, <a href="/wiki/Prehistory" title="Prehistory">prehistoric</a> man began to build useful architecture from approximately 1000 B.C. to the 15th century A.D., in the period known as the "Neo-Indian". Neo-Indian architecture consisted of incipient constructions, such as <a href="/wiki/Terrace_(earthworks)" title="Terrace (earthworks)">agricultural terraces</a> and vaults lined by stones, called mintoyes, which were used as tombs and silos for the storage of agricultural products. The Indo-Hispanic architecture is the one that begins to develop from the year 1498 A.D.<sup id="cite_ref-376" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-376">&#91;376&#93;</a></sup> Venezuelan colonial architecture is built from the <a href="/wiki/16th_century" title="16th century">16th century</a>, when Venezuela began to be a dependent colony of the <a href="/wiki/Spanish_Empire" title="Spanish Empire">Spanish Empire</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-377" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-377">&#91;377&#93;</a></sup> until 1810, when the process of Venezuelan independence began.
</p>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Cuartel_Mariano_Montilla.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/Cuartel_Mariano_Montilla.jpg/235px-Cuartel_Mariano_Montilla.jpg" decoding="async" width="235" height="176" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/Cuartel_Mariano_Montilla.jpg/353px-Cuartel_Mariano_Montilla.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/Cuartel_Mariano_Montilla.jpg/470px-Cuartel_Mariano_Montilla.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2048" data-file-height="1536" /></a><figcaption>Mariano Montilla Barracks, La Victoria, <a href="/wiki/Aragua_State" class="mw-redirect" title="Aragua State">Aragua State</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The architecture of this period is characterized by its discreet modesty. The explanation lies in the socioeconomic conditions of the <a href="/wiki/Country" title="Country">country</a>. Venezuela did not offer then to the colonizers the immense riches kept by nature for later times. The simplification of technical problems, the renunciation of most of the decorative elements and variegated ostentations of fanciful baroque, the impossibility of using <a href="/wiki/Cost" title="Cost">expensive</a> materials and the consequent lack of craftsmen, contributed to establish a modest but well-defined physiognomy of the colonial architecture of Venezuela. During the <a href="/wiki/Colonialism" title="Colonialism">colonial</a> period, there were eventually confrontations between the Spanish conquerors and the barbarians that sailed along the Venezuelan coasts, in order to take over the provinces located on the coasts of the country.
</p>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Iglesia_San_Martin_de_Tours_II.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/Iglesia_San_Martin_de_Tours_II.jpg/238px-Iglesia_San_Martin_de_Tours_II.jpg" decoding="async" width="238" height="160" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/Iglesia_San_Martin_de_Tours_II.jpg/357px-Iglesia_San_Martin_de_Tours_II.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/Iglesia_San_Martin_de_Tours_II.jpg/476px-Iglesia_San_Martin_de_Tours_II.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4327" data-file-height="2912" /></a><figcaption>St. Martin of Tours Catholic Church, built by German immigrants<sup id="cite_ref-378" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-378">&#91;378&#93;</a></sup> in Venezuela</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Christians" title="Christians">Christian</a> temples from the colonial era were constituted by an almost invariable, arrangement consisting of a rectangular plan, three naves separated by arches of alfarje roofing composed of religious architecture in colonial times. The Venezuelan society dedicated a great amount of resources to erect religious monuments comparable to those of other countries of the continent. The XVII century was of reconstruction of the <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church" title="Catholic Church">Catholic churches</a> that had been destroyed by the earthquake of 1641. In the 18th century, specifically between 1728 and 1785, the prosperity that Venezuela enjoyed due to the opening of the Compañía Guipuzcoana<sup id="cite_ref-379" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-379">&#91;379&#93;</a></sup> was also reflected in the construction of new architecture, especially of a religious nature.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Art">Art</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_art" title="Venezuelan art">Venezuelan art</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Antonio_Herrera_Toro_Autoretrato_1880.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Antonio_Herrera_Toro_Autoretrato_1880.JPG/170px-Antonio_Herrera_Toro_Autoretrato_1880.JPG" decoding="async" width="170" height="214" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Antonio_Herrera_Toro_Autoretrato_1880.JPG/255px-Antonio_Herrera_Toro_Autoretrato_1880.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Antonio_Herrera_Toro_Autoretrato_1880.JPG/340px-Antonio_Herrera_Toro_Autoretrato_1880.JPG 2x" data-file-width="438" data-file-height="551" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Antonio_Herrera_Toro" title="Antonio Herrera Toro">Antonio Herrera Toro</a>, self portrait 1880</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_art" title="Venezuelan art">Venezuelan art</a> was initially dominated by religious motifs. However, in the late 19th century, artists began emphasizing historical and heroic representations of the country's struggle for independence.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTENg200431_380-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTENg200431-380">&#91;380&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEAponte200845_381-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAponte200845-381">&#91;381&#93;</a></sup> This move was led by <a href="/wiki/Mart%C3%ADn_Tovar_y_Tovar" title="Martín Tovar y Tovar">Martín Tovar y Tovar</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEAponte200845_381-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAponte200845-381">&#91;381&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTETarverFrederick200610_382-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTETarverFrederick200610-382">&#91;382&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Modernism" title="Modernism">Modernism</a> took over in the 20th century.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTETarverFrederick200610_382-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTETarverFrederick200610-382">&#91;382&#93;</a></sup> Notable <a href="/wiki/List_of_Venezuelan_artists" title="List of Venezuelan artists">Venezuelan artists</a> include <a href="/wiki/Arturo_Michelena" title="Arturo Michelena">Arturo Michelena</a>, <a href="/wiki/Crist%C3%B3bal_Rojas_(artist)" title="Cristóbal Rojas (artist)">Cristóbal Rojas</a>, <a href="/wiki/Armando_Rever%C3%B3n" title="Armando Reverón">Armando Reverón</a>, <a href="/wiki/Manuel_Cabr%C3%A9" title="Manuel Cabré">Manuel Cabré</a>; the <a href="/wiki/Kinetic_art" title="Kinetic art">kinetic artists</a> <a href="/wiki/Jes%C3%BAs-Rafael_Soto" class="mw-redirect" title="Jesús-Rafael Soto">Jesús Soto</a>, <a href="/wiki/Gego" title="Gego">Gego</a> and <a href="/wiki/Carlos_Cruz-Diez" title="Carlos Cruz-Diez">Carlos Cruz-Diez</a>;<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTETarverFrederick200610_382-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTETarverFrederick200610-382">&#91;382&#93;</a></sup> and contemporary artists such as <a href="/wiki/Marisol_Escobar" title="Marisol Escobar">Marisol</a> and <a href="/wiki/Yucef_Merhi" title="Yucef Merhi">Yucef Merhi</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEFichner-Ratus2012519_383-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFichner-Ratus2012519-383">&#91;383&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-384" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-384">&#91;384&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Literature">Literature</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_literature" title="Venezuelan literature">Venezuelan literature</a></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_literature" title="Venezuelan literature">Venezuelan literature</a> originated soon after the Spanish conquest of the mostly pre-literate indigenous societies.<sup id="cite_ref-385" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-385">&#91;385&#93;</a></sup> It was originally dominated by <a href="/wiki/Culture_of_Spain" title="Culture of Spain">Spanish influences</a>.  Following the rise of political literature during the Venezuelan War of Independence, Venezuelan <a href="/wiki/Romanticism" title="Romanticism">Romanticism</a>, notably expounded by Juan Vicente González, emerged as the first important genre in the region. Although mainly focused on narrative writing, Venezuelan literature was advanced by poets such as <a href="/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_Eloy_Blanco" title="Andrés Eloy Blanco">Andrés Eloy Blanco</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ferm%C3%ADn_Toro" title="Fermín Toro">Fermín Toro</a>.
</p><p>Major writers and novelists include <a href="/wiki/R%C3%B3mulo_Gallegos" title="Rómulo Gallegos">Rómulo Gallegos</a>, <a href="/wiki/Teresa_de_la_Parra" title="Teresa de la Parra">Teresa de la Parra</a>, <a href="/wiki/Arturo_Uslar_Pietri" title="Arturo Uslar Pietri">Arturo Uslar Pietri</a>, <a href="/wiki/Adriano_Gonz%C3%A1lez_Le%C3%B3n" title="Adriano González León">Adriano González León</a>, <a href="/wiki/Miguel_Otero_Silva" title="Miguel Otero Silva">Miguel Otero Silva</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Mariano_Pic%C3%B3n_Salas" title="Mariano Picón Salas">Mariano Picón Salas</a>. The great poet and humanist <a href="/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_Bello" title="Andrés Bello">Andrés Bello</a> was also an educator and intellectual (He was also a childhood tutor and mentor of <a href="/wiki/Sim%C3%B3n_Bol%C3%ADvar" title="Simón Bolívar">Simón Bolívar</a>). Others, such as <a href="/wiki/Laureano_Vallenilla_Lanz" title="Laureano Vallenilla Lanz">Laureano Vallenilla Lanz</a> and <a href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Gil_Fortoul" title="José Gil Fortoul">José Gil Fortoul</a>, contributed to Venezuelan <a href="/wiki/Positivism" title="Positivism">Positivism</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Music">Music</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Music_of_Venezuela" title="Music of Venezuela">Music of Venezuela</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:2952-Danzas_Guanaguanare_de_Venezuela_no_Festival_folclorico_da_Coru%C3%B1a._(8200095256).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/63/2952-Danzas_Guanaguanare_de_Venezuela_no_Festival_folclorico_da_Coru%C3%B1a._%288200095256%29.jpg/220px-2952-Danzas_Guanaguanare_de_Venezuela_no_Festival_folclorico_da_Coru%C3%B1a._%288200095256%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="173" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/63/2952-Danzas_Guanaguanare_de_Venezuela_no_Festival_folclorico_da_Coru%C3%B1a._%288200095256%29.jpg/330px-2952-Danzas_Guanaguanare_de_Venezuela_no_Festival_folclorico_da_Coru%C3%B1a._%288200095256%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/63/2952-Danzas_Guanaguanare_de_Venezuela_no_Festival_folclorico_da_Coru%C3%B1a._%288200095256%29.jpg/440px-2952-Danzas_Guanaguanare_de_Venezuela_no_Festival_folclorico_da_Coru%C3%B1a._%288200095256%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1824" data-file-height="1432" /></a><figcaption>The Guanaguanare dance, a popular dance in <a href="/wiki/Portuguesa_(state)" title="Portuguesa (state)">Portuguesa State</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The indigenous musical styles of Venezuela are exemplified by groups like Un Sólo Pueblo and <a href="/wiki/Serenata_Guayanesa" title="Serenata Guayanesa">Serenata Guayanesa</a>. The national musical instrument is the <a href="/wiki/Cuatro_(Venezuela)" title="Cuatro (Venezuela)">cuatro</a>. Traditional musical styles and songs mainly emerged in and around the <i>llanos</i> region, including, "Alma llanera" (by <a href="/wiki/Pedro_El%C3%ADas_Guti%C3%A9rrez" title="Pedro Elías Gutiérrez">Pedro Elías Gutiérrez</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rafael_Bol%C3%ADvar_Coronado" title="Rafael Bolívar Coronado">Rafael Bolívar Coronado</a>), "Florentino y el diablo" (by <a href="/wiki/Alberto_Arvelo_Torrealba" title="Alberto Arvelo Torrealba">Alberto Arvelo Torrealba</a>), "Concierto en la llanura" by <a href="/wiki/Juan_Vicente_Torrealba" title="Juan Vicente Torrealba">Juan Vicente Torrealba</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Caballo_Viejo" title="Caballo Viejo">"Caballo viejo"</a> (by <a href="/wiki/Sim%C3%B3n_D%C3%ADaz" title="Simón Díaz">Simón Díaz</a>).
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Gaita_zuliana" title="Gaita zuliana">Zulian gaita</a> is also a very popular genre, generally performed during Christmas. The national dance is the <a href="/wiki/Joropo" title="Joropo">joropo</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECortés20132134_386-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECortés20132134-386">&#91;386&#93;</a></sup> Venezuela has always been a melting pot of cultures and this can be seen in the richness and variety of its musical styles and dances: <a href="/wiki/Calypso_music" title="Calypso music">calipso</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bambuco" title="Bambuco">bambuco</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ful%C3%ADa" title="Fulía">fulía</a>, cantos de pilado de maíz, cantos de lavanderas, sebucán, and maremare.<sup id="cite_ref-387" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-387">&#91;387&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Teresa_Carre%C3%B1o" title="Teresa Carreño">Teresa Carreño</a> was a world-famous 19th century piano virtuoso. Recently, great classical music performances have come out of Venezuela. The <a href="/wiki/Sim%C3%B3n_Bol%C3%ADvar_Youth_Orchestra" class="mw-redirect" title="Simón Bolívar Youth Orchestra">Simón Bolívar Youth Orchestra</a> has hosted a number of excellent concerts in many European concert halls, most notably at the 2007 London <a href="/wiki/The_Proms" class="mw-redirect" title="The Proms">Proms</a>, and has received several honors. The orchestra is the pinnacle of <a href="/wiki/El_Sistema" title="El Sistema">El Sistema</a>, a publicly financed, voluntary music education program now being emulated in other countries.
</p><p>In the early 21st century, a movement known as "Movida Acústica Urbana" featured musicians trying to save some national traditions, creating their own original songs but using traditional instruments.<sup id="cite_ref-388" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-388">&#91;388&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-389" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-389">&#91;389&#93;</a></sup> Some groups following this movement are Tambor Urbano,<sup id="cite_ref-390" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-390">&#91;390&#93;</a></sup> Los Sinverguenzas, C4Trío, and Orozco Jam.<sup id="cite_ref-391" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-391">&#91;391&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Afro-Venezuelan musical traditions are most intimately related to the festivals of the "black folk saints" San Juan and <a href="/wiki/Benedict_the_Moor" title="Benedict the Moor">St. Benedict the Moor</a>. Specific songs are related to the different stages of their festivals and processions, when the saints start their yearly "<i>paseo"</i> – stroll – through the community.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Sport">Sport</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Sport_in_Venezuela" title="Sport in Venezuela">Sport in Venezuela</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Baseball_in_Venezuela" title="Baseball in Venezuela">Baseball in Venezuela</a> and <a href="/wiki/Football_in_Venezuela" title="Football in Venezuela">Football in Venezuela</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Venezuela_national_baseball_team_on_November_7,_2015.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/62/Venezuela_national_baseball_team_on_November_7%2C_2015.jpg/220px-Venezuela_national_baseball_team_on_November_7%2C_2015.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="148" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/62/Venezuela_national_baseball_team_on_November_7%2C_2015.jpg/330px-Venezuela_national_baseball_team_on_November_7%2C_2015.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/62/Venezuela_national_baseball_team_on_November_7%2C_2015.jpg/440px-Venezuela_national_baseball_team_on_November_7%2C_2015.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2600" data-file-height="1750" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Venezuela_national_baseball_team" title="Venezuela national baseball team">Venezuela national baseball team</a> in 2015</figcaption></figure>
<p>The origins of baseball in Venezuela are unclear, although it is known that the sport was being played in the country by the late 19th century.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTENicholsMorse2010306_392-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTENicholsMorse2010306-392">&#91;392&#93;</a></sup> In the early 20th century, North American immigrants who came to Venezuela to work in the nation's oil industry helped to popularize the sport in Venezuela.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEWardrope200337_393-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWardrope200337-393">&#91;393&#93;</a></sup> During the 1930s, baseball's popularity continued to rise in the country, leading to the foundation of the <a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_Professional_Baseball_League" title="Venezuelan Professional Baseball League">Venezuelan Professional Baseball League</a> (LVBP) in 1945, and the sport would soon become the nation's most popular.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEJozsa201312_394-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJozsa201312-394">&#91;394&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGibson200618_395-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGibson200618-395">&#91;395&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The popularity of baseball in the country makes Venezuela a rarity among its South American neighbors—association football is the dominant sport in the continent.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEWardrope200337_393-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWardrope200337-393">&#91;393&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGibson200618_395-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGibson200618-395">&#91;395&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTENicholsMorse2010307_396-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTENicholsMorse2010307-396">&#91;396&#93;</a></sup> However, football, as well as <a href="/wiki/Basketball" title="Basketball">basketball</a>, are among the more popular sports played in Venezuela.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEAalgaard200454_397-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAalgaard200454-397">&#91;397&#93;</a></sup> Venezuela hosted the <a href="/wiki/2012_FIBA_World_Olympic_Qualifying_Tournament_for_Men" title="2012 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament for Men">2012 Basketball World Olympic Qualifying Tournament</a> and the <a href="/wiki/FIBA_Americas_Championship" class="mw-redirect" title="FIBA Americas Championship">2013 FIBA Basketball Americas Championship</a>, which took place in the <a href="/wiki/Poliedro_de_Caracas" title="Poliedro de Caracas">Poliedro de Caracas</a>.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Venezuela-guinea_cropped.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Venezuela-guinea_cropped.jpg/220px-Venezuela-guinea_cropped.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="123" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Venezuela-guinea_cropped.jpg/330px-Venezuela-guinea_cropped.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Venezuela-guinea_cropped.jpg/440px-Venezuela-guinea_cropped.jpg 2x" data-file-width="770" data-file-height="429" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Venezuela_national_football_team" title="Venezuela national football team">Venezuela national football team</a>, popularly known as the "Vinotinto"</figcaption></figure>
<p>Although not as popular in Venezuela as the rest of South America, football, spearheaded by the <a href="/wiki/Venezuela_national_football_team" title="Venezuela national football team">Venezuela national football team</a> is gaining popularity as well. The sport is also noted for having an increased focus during the World Cup.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEAalgaard200454_397-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAalgaard200454-397">&#91;397&#93;</a></sup> Venezuela is scheduled to host the <a href="/wiki/Copa_Am%C3%A9rica" title="Copa América">Copa América</a> every 40 years.<sup id="cite_ref-398" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-398">&#91;398&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Venezuela is also home to former <a href="/wiki/Formula_1" class="mw-redirect" title="Formula 1">Formula 1</a> driver, <a href="/wiki/Pastor_Maldonado" title="Pastor Maldonado">Pastor Maldonado</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Strickland2015_399-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Strickland2015-399">&#91;399&#93;</a></sup> Maldonado has increased the reception of Formula 1 in Venezuela, helping to popularize the sport in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-400" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-400">&#91;400&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In the <a href="/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics" title="2012 Summer Olympics">2012 Summer Olympics</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rub%C3%A9n_Limardo" title="Rubén Limardo">Rubén Limardo</a> won a gold medal in <a href="/wiki/Fencing_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics" title="Fencing at the 2012 Summer Olympics">fencing</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-401" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-401">&#91;401&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In the Winter Sports, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Cesar_Baena&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Cesar Baena (page does not exist)">Cesar Baena</a> had represented the country since 2008 in Nordic Skiing, the first South American skier to compete in a FIS Cross Country Ski World Cup on Düsseldorf 2009.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Cuisine">Cuisine</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_cuisine" title="Venezuelan cuisine">Venezuelan cuisine</a></div>
<div class="excerpt-block"><style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1066933788">.mw-parser-output .excerpt-hat .mw-editsection-like{font-style:normal}</style><div class="excerpt">
<a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_cuisine" title="Venezuelan cuisine">Venezuelan cuisine</a> is influenced by its European (<a href="/wiki/Italy" title="Italy">Italian</a>, <a href="/wiki/Spain" title="Spain">Spanish</a>, <a href="/wiki/Portugal" title="Portugal">Portuguese</a>, and <a href="/wiki/France" title="France">French</a>), West African, and indigenous traditions. Venezuelan cuisine varies greatly from one region to another. <a href="/wiki/Food_staple" class="mw-redirect" title="Food staple">Food staples</a> include <a href="/wiki/Maize" title="Maize">corn</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rice" title="Rice">rice</a>, <a href="/wiki/Plantain_(cooking)" class="mw-redirect" title="Plantain (cooking)">plantains</a>, <a href="/wiki/Yam_(vegetable)" title="Yam (vegetable)">yams</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bean" title="Bean">beans</a> and several meats. Potatoes, tomatoes, <a href="/wiki/Onion" title="Onion">onions</a>, <a href="/wiki/Eggplant" title="Eggplant">eggplants</a>, <a href="/wiki/Squash_(plant)" class="mw-redirect" title="Squash (plant)">squashes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Spinach" title="Spinach">spinach</a> and <a href="/wiki/Zucchini" title="Zucchini">zucchini</a> are also common side dishes in the Venezuelan diet. <a href="/wiki/Aj%C3%AD_dulce" title="Ají dulce">Ají dulce</a> and <a href="/wiki/Papel%C3%B3n" class="mw-redirect" title="Papelón">papelón</a> are found in most recipes. <a href="/wiki/Worcestershire_sauce" title="Worcestershire sauce">Worcestershire sauce</a> is also used frequently in stews. Venezuela is also known for having a large variety of white cheese (<a href="/wiki/Queso_blanco" title="Queso blanco">queso blanco</a>), usually named by geographical region.</div></div>

<li id="cite_note-321"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-321">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1133582631"><cite id="CITEREFBenítez,_Deivis2011" class="citation news cs1 cs1-prop-foreign-lang-source">Benítez, Deivis (2011) [Updated 13 August 2012]. <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://web.archive.org/web/20130116234901/http://www.minpi.gob.ve/minpi/es/noticias/1548-np1428">"Poblaciones Indígenas en aumento según censo poblacional 2011"</a> (in Spanish). PRENSA MINPPPI. Archived from <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="http://www.minpi.gob.ve/minpi/es/noticias/1548-np1428">the original</a> on 16 January 2013<span class="reference-accessdate">. Retrieved <span class="nowrap">10 October</span> 2012</span>, article text:</cite><span title="ctx_ver=Z39.88-2004&amp;rft_val_fmt=info%3Aofi%2Ffmt%3Akev%3Amtx%3Ajournal&amp;rft.genre=article&amp;rft.atitle=Poblaciones+Ind%C3%ADgenas+en+aumento+seg%C3%BAn+censo+poblacional+2011&amp;rft.date=2011&amp;rft.au=Ben%C3%ADtez%2C+Deivis&amp;rft_id=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.minpi.gob.ve%2Fminpi%2Fes%2Fnoticias%2F1548-np1428&amp;rfr_id=info%3Asid%2Fen.wikipedia.org%3AVenezuela" class="Z3988"></span><span class="cs1-maint citation-comment"><code class="cs1-code">{{<a href="/wiki/Template:Cite_news" title="Template:Cite news">cite news</a>}}</code>:  CS1 maint: postscript (<a href="/wiki/Category:CS1_maint:_postscript" title="Category:CS1 maint: postscript">link</a>)</span><style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1127642053">.mw-parser-output .hidden-begin{box-sizing:border-box;width:100%;padding:5px;border:none;font-size:95%}.mw-parser-output .hidden-title{font-weight:bold;line-height:1.6;text-align:left}.mw-parser-output .hidden-content{text-align:left}</style><div class="hidden-begin mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="border:none;"><div class="hidden-title" style="text-align:center;"></div><div class="hidden-content mw-collapsible-content" style="">
<i>Los resultados arrojados por el censo poblacional realizado por el Instituto Nacional de Estadísticas en el 2011 demuestra que las poblaciones indígenas ha aumentado progresivamente con respecto al censo del año 2001.</i><br />Según los datos estadísticos publicados por el INE, el total de población que se declaró indígena por sexo, arrojó un resultado de 50,46% hombre y 49,54% mujeres representando 365.920 hombres y 359.208 mujeres para un total de 725.148 personas que se declararon indígenas de Venezuela.<br />Así mismo, se tomó el porcentaje de población por entidad donde el estado Zulia es la entidad con más indígenas con un 61%, seguido del estado Amazonas con 10%, Bolívar con un 8%, Delta Amacuro con 6%, Anzoátegui 5%, Sucre 3%, Apure y Monagas 2% mientras que en otras entidades existe un 3% de población indígena.<br />Entre tanto, los pueblos indígenas con mayor población se encuentran los Wayuu 58%, Warao 7%, Kariña 5%, Pemón 4%, Piaroa, Jivi, Añu, Cumanágoto 3%, Yukpa, Chaima 2%, el pueblo Yanomami 1% y otros pueblos con un 9%.</div></div></span>
</li>
